haystack_sessions.content: The current hesitation-label field uses HOLD in this fictional teaching corpus.
I will record HOLD as the working hesitation tag.
The corpus is project-authored example dialogue, not authentic participant speech.
I will preserve that fictional provenance.
We created the first annotation spreadsheet.
Spreadsheet creation is complete; annotation review is not.

Annotation desk memorandum A. Alongside the hesitation convention, we are organizing a small fictional demonstration corpus with three independent work lists: clip boundaries, descriptive metadata and a future teaching exercise. The first spreadsheet has a row for each invented clip, but its columns are not yet suitable for exchange with another class. The current columns are Clip, Length, Language and Comment. Length does not specify a unit, and Comment combines recording notes with teaching suggestions. Before anyone imports the table, we should separate these meanings. This is a schema problem, not evidence that any audio boundary is correct.

I propose using milliseconds for the numeric duration column and a separate free-text note for unresolved boundary questions. The instructor has not approved that choice. A student asked whether a value written as 1.5 would mean seconds or minutes; this illustrates why the existing column is ambiguous. We have not converted the values already in the sheet. The two clips awaiting duration checks remain unresolved. Other rows have empty duration cells rather than zeroes. Empty means not measured; zero would be a measured value and must not be used as a convenient replacement.

The descriptive metadata will identify the imagined setting and intended teaching difficulty. It must not invent real fieldwork locations, speaker consent or demographic survey results. I drafted three setting categories: classroom exchange, market conversation and travel enquiry. These are fictional scene types, not statements about where recordings were obtained. The examples currently have improvised notes rather than agreed categories. A separate review is needed to decide whether the categories are useful for lesson planning. No student has been assigned a category-labeling task yet.

For the teaching exercise, the instructor wants students to compare two annotated examples and explain a disagreement in their reasoning. That is a future activity, not a measurement of agreement. We need an answer-discussion sheet that distinguishes a label decision from uncertainty about the clip boundary. The instructor also wants the examples short enough for replay during class, but has not given a maximum duration. Please collect that requirement before selecting examples. At the next meeting we can resolve the duration unit, the metadata columns and the lesson-length constraint without claiming the fictional clips represent authentic participant speech.
The duration unit, evidence columns and lesson-length requirement remain open. Empty durations will not become zero, and no authentic field-participant claim is supported.
Before publishing an example clip, remove the speaker identifier from its file name.
Publication requires a filename with the speaker identifier removed.
We might display waveform thumbnails.
Thumbnail display is only a proposal.
The examples contain invented place names.
Those names must not be represented as real field locations.

Metadata decision note B. The instructor approved milliseconds for DurationMs and requested a separate BoundaryNote column. We will preserve the original Length column in a read-only worksheet until each existing entry has been interpreted. A blank value must remain blank during this migration. The table also needs a MigrationStatus column so another helper can distinguish reviewed conversions from untouched rows. The proposed statuses are pending, checked and needs-question. These are spreadsheet workflow states, not annotation labels for speech. The instructor approved the three status words but has not reviewed any individual row.

The two clips awaiting duration checks have been assigned to a pair of helpers. Each will listen to the same disposable copy and write their chosen start and end points independently. We are not asking them to decide the hesitation convention. Their notes should state whether leading silence is included, because that is the source of an existing ambiguity. The helpers accepted the task for the next session. Acceptance does not supply measured endpoints. No duration has yet changed in the live exchange table, and we should not populate it from an unreviewed message.

The imagined-setting categories were simplified. The instructor rejected market conversation because the current examples do not contain a transaction or price request. The remaining proposed set is classroom exchange, travel enquiry and household planning. A student suggested that household planning should mean any conversation mentioning a home; the instructor disagreed, saying the category should describe the purpose of the exchange, not an isolated noun. This distinction needs to be written into the category guidance. The guidance is still a draft and is not ready for novice annotation.

For the teaching exercise, the instructor set a target of two examples lasting no more than twenty seconds each. This is a selection limit for classroom replay, not a claim about the current clips. We cannot choose the two unmeasured examples solely because they appear short in the spreadsheet. The classroom also has one shared loudspeaker and a projector with unreliable audio, so the exercise plan should include a local playback test. That equipment test is separate from duration review and has not happened. The next useful preparation work is drafting the category guidance and arranging the helpers' endpoint comparison.
The approved schema uses milliseconds and explicit migration states. Endpoint listening, setting guidance and playback setup are assigned or proposed, not completed.
The overlap label has a separate definition from hesitation.
I will not use overlap evidence to redefine the hesitation tag.
Two invented clips need duration checks.
Their durations remain unverified.
Please prepare an annotator instruction draft.
It should separate working labels and unresolved checks.

Boundary-comparison and metadata note C. Both helpers completed their independent listening notes on disposable copies. They agreed about the end of the first example but disagreed about whether its initial silence belonged in the exercise excerpt. For the second example, one helper included a trailing chair noise and the other stopped before it. These notes are observations about boundaries, not a final edit instruction. The instructor wants the original examples preserved and asks us to create an explicit decision record before changing any endpoint. The live table still shows both checks as pending.

We wrote the first draft of the imagined-setting guidance. Classroom exchange means a discussion about a lesson or classroom task, even if the speakers mention a trip. Travel enquiry means seeking information needed for travel, rather than any reference to a station or road. Household planning concerns arranging a domestic activity. Each definition now has a fictional positive example and a near-miss example. We have not assigned those categories to the actual demonstration rows. This distinction matters because a guide can be complete while the dataset remains uncategorized.

The metadata helper tested a spreadsheet export containing four dummy rows. One row had an empty duration, one had a decimal, one contained a text note in the numeric column and one used an integer. The importer rejected the text note and preserved the empty cell, but silently rounded the decimal. We do not yet know whether that behavior is acceptable. No live corpus row was imported during the test. The decimal result should be reported to the instructor before deciding a conversion policy. A successful dummy import is not evidence that the full exchange sheet is ready.

The loudspeaker was available for a classroom test, but its connecting cable was missing. The playback test therefore did not run. A student offered a wireless speaker; the instructor has not approved it because the room connection policy is unclear. The paper exercise outline can still advance: it should ask students to separate disagreement about an annotation convention from disagreement about the boundaries of the excerpt they heard. We have not collected student answers or measured agreement. The next meeting should resolve the boundary questions and the decimal policy before anyone treats the table as a finalized teaching resource.
The helper boundary notes and dummy import findings need decisions. The missing cable prevented playback; drafted guidance has not yet categorized the examples.
Draft one instruction from the current hesitation convention.
The draft tells annotators to use HOLD for hesitation.
Keep that draft internal until review.
It is not a published guideline.
The team rejected waveform thumbnails for the small display.
The thumbnail proposal is rejected.

Instructor review record D. The instructor decided to exclude the leading silence from the first exercise excerpt and to exclude the trailing chair noise from the second. These decisions apply to the disposable teaching excerpts, while the source examples remain preserved. The helpers will implement the endpoint changes and record the resulting durations in milliseconds after replay. The decision record now names the included content rather than merely saying use the shorter version. We have not yet received confirmation that either edited excerpt has been saved or replayed.

The decimal import behavior was rejected. DurationMs must contain an integer entered after the relevant measurement decision; the importer must not silently round a decimal supplied by a helper. The developer changed the validation message so a decimal entry is flagged for review. A test using the same four dummy rows now rejects both the decimal and the text note while keeping the empty cell empty. This test establishes the revised validation behavior for those cases, not correctness of the entire metadata table. The live migration still requires a row-by-row check.

The instructor approved the imagined-setting definitions and their near-miss examples. Two students will now classify the demonstration rows independently using that guide. Their task is to flag ambiguous cases rather than force every row into one of the three categories. We added an UnresolvedSetting flag for that purpose. The flag is metadata about uncertainty, not another speech annotation label. The students have not started their assignments. The approved guide remains available as a separate document so later disagreement can be traced to a specific definition rather than memory of an oral explanation.

The room manager confirmed that a wired speaker is permitted and a wireless connection is not. We ordered a compatible cable and kept the playback test pending. The teaching outline now includes a silent reading alternative in case audio cannot be played, but the instructor has not approved it as a substitute for the listening exercise. The printed outline therefore shows it as a contingency. A future handoff should retain the difference between the intended listening task and that fallback, rather than reporting that the class completed either activity. No examples have been released outside the authoring workspace.
The boundary decisions are approved for excerpt copies, but edits are pending. The validation fix passed its dummy cases; the live migration and classroom setup still require work.
We checked the two clip durations and corrected one endpoint.
The endpoint correction is complete for that invented clip.
No examples have been published.
I will not infer public release from the duration check.
The filename scrubber is still untested.
Publication preparation remains incomplete.

Corpus preparation record E. The helpers saved the two teaching-excerpt copies after implementing the approved endpoint decisions. They replayed the copies and entered their durations as integers in the draft exchange sheet. One endpoint correction is also reflected in the original work list above. The exchange sheet has not been exported to the release folder. These local copies are preparation artifacts, not published examples. The read-only original Length worksheet remains available so another reviewer can trace how the numeric values were obtained instead of assuming every old entry was already expressed in milliseconds.

The two students completed the imagined-setting task. They agreed on three rows and marked one differently. One student chose travel enquiry for a conversation about arranging a lesson near a station; the other chose classroom exchange. The instructor referred them to the purpose-based definitions and asked for a short rationale. No majority vote has been used to erase the disagreement. We created a separate ReviewRationale cell rather than overwriting either student's first answer. This preserves the distinction between initial independent judgments and an eventual reconciled setting category.

The new cable arrived. A helper connected the wired loudspeaker to the classroom computer and confirmed that a local test tone played. They have not played the two demonstration excerpts in the actual lesson room. The successful tone test confirms a connection, not audibility of quiet speech from the back row. The instructor requested a second test with one of the disposable excerpts and asked the listener to sit in the rear corner. That test is scheduled but has not happened. The wireless speaker remains an unapproved alternative and should not appear in the current equipment plan.

The instructor accepted the printed exercise questions and asked for a facilitator note explaining how to handle an unresolved boundary objection. The facilitator should acknowledge the objection, identify which excerpt version was used and keep that issue separate from a disagreement about the target annotation convention. This note is still being drafted. The class itself has not run, so there are no participant scores or agreement statistics to insert into the handoff. A useful next check is whether the draft exchange sheet contains the approved units and preserved rationale fields before any release preparation begins.
Two local excerpts now exist, but no public release is implied. The setting disagreement and rear-corner playback check remain open, with the facilitator note still being drafted.
The overlap definition passed review without changes.
That review does not independently approve the hesitation convention.
We tested the filename scrubber on a disposable copy.
A test on a copy does not prove every release file was cleaned.
The original clip files remain in the authoring folder.
Authoring and release copies should stay distinct.

Review and validation note F. The instructor resolved the disputed imagined-setting row as classroom exchange because the conversation's purpose is arranging a lesson; the station is incidental context. We retained both initial student choices and their rationales in the review worksheet. The reconciled category is stored in a separate FinalSetting column. This makes the process traceable without implying the two students originally agreed. The other three rows retain their matching decisions. These four rows are a classroom demonstration, not a measured estimate of how reliably people label a real corpus.

The metadata helper reviewed the migration statuses. Three rows have checked integer durations and one row remains needs-question because the original entry had no interpretable unit. We did not replace that missing measurement with an average or copy another clip's length. The importer can accept an empty duration with that status, but the lesson-selection filter must exclude the row until the duration limit can be checked. The filter is a new proposed tool and has not yet been tested. The current selected exercise pair consists only of the two locally replayed excerpt copies.

The rear-corner audio test found that the quieter excerpt was difficult to hear at the initial volume. Increasing the volume made both excerpts intelligible to the helper without distortion on that test. The helper recorded the device position and volume setting in the room checklist. This is a limited observation from one test position, not a guarantee about every learner's hearing. The instructor requested that the facilitator ask the class whether playback is audible before beginning. We have not conducted the class or collected those responses.

The facilitator note now contains the excerpt-version check and a place to record unresolved questions. The instructor approved this note for the planned teaching exercise. That approval does not release the example clips or establish that all release filenames meet the publication condition. The filename scrubber was tested separately on a disposable copy, and the authoring files remain distinct from any prospective release copies. The next preparation work is testing the lesson-selection filter and assembling a manifest that refers to exact excerpt versions, so a later coordinator does not accidentally replay an earlier boundary draft.
The reconciled category preserves the initial disagreement. One duration row remains unresolved; the selected pair and tested room settings do not establish a completed class or released files.
Retain the old annotator draft for version comparison.
An old instruction should not override the current label field.
The release folder is still empty.
There is no published clip to count.
We planned an inter-annotator exercise but have not run it.
A planned exercise is not agreement evidence.

Selection-filter test record G. We tested the proposed lesson-selection filter on a dummy table with three cases: a checked duration below the classroom limit, a checked duration above it, and an empty duration marked needs-question. It selected only the first case. A fourth case used a short duration marked pending; the filter initially selected it too, which was wrong because measurement review had not finished. The developer changed the condition to require checked status as well as an acceptable duration. A repeat of all four cases produced the intended selections. These are tool tests, not new corpus measurements.

The dry-run lesson manifest now lists the two locally replayed excerpt versions and the approved facilitator note. It is stored in the authoring workspace, while the release folder remains empty. The manifest does not contain the example audio itself. It includes a field for the future release filename, deliberately left blank until the publication condition is checked. A helper suggested filling those blanks with the current authoring filenames to make the table look complete. We rejected that suggestion because a visually complete manifest could hide unfinished release preparation.

The room checklist carries the tested speaker position and volume setting, plus the instruction to ask about audibility before starting. The class date is still being arranged. The printed silent-reading fallback is retained but marked contingency, and no one should report it as the completed activity. The instructor asked the next facilitator to bring spare paper for written rationales. We have set aside six blank sheets in the teaching folder. This supply count is independent of the number of example clips and must not be reported as a count of participant responses.

The unresolved duration row remains excluded from the exercise pair. The next measurement helper should establish its unit from the preserved original note or remeasure the relevant copy; they should not infer a value from the column's new name. The reconciled imagined-setting category is complete for the four reviewed rows, with initial disagreements still visible. An incoming coordinator can therefore advance metadata cleanup, classroom logistics or release checks independently. None of those achievements supplies real participant consent, measured annotator agreement or proof that the planned teaching exercise has taken place.
The filter now rejects pending short values. The authoring manifest has deliberate blank release fields, the class remains unrun, and six sheets are supplies rather than responses.
Prepare a handoff for the next annotation lead.
It can separate working tags, version history and publication preparation.
Do not claim participant consent or measured agreement.
Neither exists for these fictional examples.
Suggest one next release check.
Check the final release filenames for speaker identifiers before publication.

Annotation lead handoff H. Use the draft exchange table with DurationMs, BoundaryNote, MigrationStatus and FinalSetting. Do not import the old Length worksheet as though all its values were milliseconds. Three reviewed rows have checked integer durations; the remaining needs-question row stays unselected until its measurement is resolved. The selection filter has passed the four described dummy cases, including the important distinction between a short pending value and a short checked value. That limited test evidence should travel with the filter script so the next helper understands which behavior was examined.

The teaching pair uses the two replayed local excerpt versions, not the early boundary drafts. The instructor approved their boundary decisions and the facilitator note, and the room checklist records a rear-corner playback test. The class has not run. Six blank rationale sheets are supplies, not six responses. The plan still requires an audibility check with the actual class before the exercise starts. If the wired speaker cannot be used, the facilitator must obtain a decision about the reading contingency rather than silently claiming it is equivalent to the listening activity.

The imagined-setting review preserves the original student choices, their rationales and the instructor's reconciled category. One initially disputed row was resolved by the purpose of the exchange rather than the incidental mention of a station. That example should remain in the guidance, because it explains a real decision rule used in this fictional teaching workflow. It is not evidence that a real population has a particular annotation skill. The corpus and every example remain explicitly invented instructional material, with no field-participant testimony or consent record implied.

The dry-run manifest is in the authoring workspace and the release folder remains empty. Future release-filename cells are intentionally blank; replacing them with authoring filenames would conceal a required check. A useful next task is to compare the manifest's excerpt versions with the approved boundary record and to assign an owner for each unfinished release field. Another is resolving the outstanding duration row without guessing its unit. These tasks are independently useful even while a working annotation convention changes. Preserve the distinction between an approved instruction, a tested helper tool, a prepared artifact and an actual publication when completing the next handoff.
The next lead can verify excerpt versions against the manifest or resolve the outstanding duration unit. Classroom approval, helper-tool tests and publication remain distinct milestones.

haystack_sessions.content: The unclaimed blue crates are assigned to Shelf Lantern in our demonstration storeroom.
I will record Shelf Lantern for the unclaimed blue crates.
The red crates belong to a separate school collection.
I will not combine those crate assignments.
We assembled empty boxes yesterday.
Box assembly is complete, not packing.

Sorting desk record A. We are preparing three demonstration craft boxes for a school activity, separately from the crate holding arrangements. The boxes are named Paper Kit, Texture Kit and Drawing Kit. These are temporary kit identifiers, not recipient names. Paper Kit is intended to contain folding paper and sample envelopes; Texture Kit contains fabric scraps and cardboard strips; Drawing Kit contains blunt pencils and blank cards. The teacher has asked us to avoid glitter because it is difficult to remove from the classroom floor. That request has been accepted, and glitter must not be quietly added as a decorative extra.

The teacher has not confirmed how many children will attend. We therefore cannot claim that the quantities in any proposed kit are sufficient for the whole class. A volunteer suggested writing serves twenty on every box, but we rejected that wording because it would imply an unsupported attendance and allocation calculation. The current labels should identify the contents only. We need a separate planning line for the attendance estimate when the teacher supplies it. No completed box comparison or dispatch has occurred at this opening stage.

We have two reusable trolleys for moving demonstration supplies inside the storeroom. One has a wheel that catches when turned sharply, and the other rolls smoothly on the clear central aisle. The faulty trolley has been set aside with a handwritten warning. Nobody has assessed whether its wheel can be repaired. The working trolley is shared with another community group after lunch, so our packing plan cannot assume it remains available all day. Carrying boxes by hand is a possible alternative, but the coordinator wants a weight and route check before choosing that option.

Volunteer access is another unfinished task. The morning helper knows the packing method, while the afternoon helper is new and has not received the sorting brief. I drafted a one-page orientation describing kit identifiers, the no-glitter decision and where to record discrepancies. It is not signed off yet. The coordinator wants the new helper to demonstrate the recording procedure using an empty practice box before handling live kits. This is a proposed training check, not evidence that the helper has completed it. The kit content plan, trolley issue and orientation draft can be advanced without revealing any restricted crate location.
I will preserve the separate kit plans, trolley problem and orientation task. The unknown attendance and unfinished comparisons prevent any class-sufficiency or dispatch claim.
Before a sealed box enters the dispatch pile, its item list must match its box label.
Dispatch preparation requires the item-list and box-label match.
Someone suggested sorting by lid color alone.
Lid color is only a proposal, not the required check.
All demonstration contents are classroom craft supplies.
I will not describe them as medicine or food.

School request and equipment note B. The teacher confirmed a class of eighteen children and asked for pairs to share materials at nine work tables. This changes the planning basis from an unknown class size to nine shared stations. It does not establish the quantities already packed. We should record the table count separately from the number of children, because a helper could otherwise assemble eighteen full station sets. The teacher also asked for large blank cards instead of small ones in Drawing Kit so two children can draw together. The contents plan has been revised, but the physical cards have not been swapped.

The coordinator reviewed the orientation draft and requested an example discrepancy. We added a fictional practice case in which a box label says plain envelopes while the item list says window envelopes. The correct response is to stop and ask which item is intended, not to rewrite the list merely to make the two documents agree. This example is about recording an inconsistency, not a claim that any live kit has that specific problem. The new helper will practice it next session. Their access remains supervised until the coordinator observes the exercise.

A maintenance volunteer inspected the faulty trolley and found a bent wheel bracket. They recommend replacing the bracket rather than tightening the wheel bolt. That is an assessment and recommendation; no repair has been performed. We have asked whether a compatible part is available. The working trolley remains shared after lunch, and the packing schedule must account for its availability. The coordinator ruled out lifting a closed box by one of its lid flaps, because that flap is not designed as a carrying handle. That handling instruction should appear in the orientation before anyone practices moving a kit.

The teacher has not yet given a collection contact or vehicle arrangement. We may prepare a transport inquiry, but no pickup appointment exists. Please do not treat the school attendance confirmation as a delivery confirmation. The next useful work is replacing the small cards in the contents plan and checking the actual stock of large cards. The afternoon helper can also practice discrepancy reporting with the empty box. Keep training observations, equipment repair status and live kit checks on separate lines so an improvement in one area does not falsely close another unfinished task.
The plan now uses nine shared stations for eighteen children. Large-card stock, training, bracket compatibility and collection arrangements still need their own checks.
The school collected the red crates.
That collection does not establish pickup of the blue crates.
We found a box with a missing item list.
It cannot satisfy the matching check yet.
Please draft a sorting reminder.
The reminder can distinguish completed collections and unresolved packing.

Inventory and training record C. A stock check found enough large blank cards for nine shared drawing stations, with four extra cards available for demonstrations. The teacher approved using one extra card to show the exercise and keeping the other three as spares. The small cards remain unused stock for another activity; they are not waste and should not be counted as missing from Drawing Kit. We have updated the contents plan to distinguish station supplies, demonstration material and spare stock. This is still a packing plan, not a certified match between any closed box and its paperwork.

The new helper completed the empty-box discrepancy exercise under supervision. They correctly noticed the plain-versus-window-envelope mismatch, wrote a question in the practice log and waited for a decision. They also lifted the empty box from beneath rather than from its lid flap. The coordinator approved them to assist with live packing while another helper checks their written records. This is a limited training sign-off, not a declaration that all later packing work will be error-free. We retained the practice sheet as training evidence and marked it clearly so it cannot be mistaken for an unresolved live-kit discrepancy.

During preparation we found that Texture Kit had no item list in its document pocket. The lid label remained attached. The missing list has been reported to the coordinator, and the box is outside the dispatch pile. We should not reconstruct the list solely from the label, because that would remove the independent comparison. The teacher's approved contents plan and the packing helper's notes are available for producing a replacement list. Nobody has yet done that replacement or compared it with the label. The other kits retain their own document pockets.

The maintenance volunteer located a possible trolley bracket but needs to confirm its dimensions before ordering. The part is not in our inventory. The working trolley is available for a later morning slot, so the coordinator tentatively scheduled a supervised movement rehearsal with empty boxes. A tentative schedule is not a completed rehearsal or a vehicle booking. The next shift should check the bracket dimensions, produce the missing list from independent packing notes and record the teacher's still-pending collection contact. None of these actions changes the separate crate assignment or authorizes a guessed recipient for unclaimed material.
The helper completed a practice exercise, not live certification. Texture Kit lacks its list, and the other preparation records do not substitute for that missing evidence.
Draft a retrieval note for the unclaimed blue crates.
The draft directs the sorter to Shelf Lantern for those crates.
That note is not permission for public access to the storeroom.
I will keep its intended internal purpose.
The lid-color proposal was rejected after mixed lids were found.
The required matching rule remains unchanged.

Packing exception record D. The teacher confirmed the large-card arrangement and clarified that the sample envelopes in Paper Kit must be unsealed. Children will use them to practice folding and inserting messages, so sealed envelopes would not support the planned activity. The existing contents plan simply said envelopes. We amended that description and retained the earlier wording in the change log. This is a meaningful content clarification, not permission to certify an already packed box without opening it. The helper must verify the envelope condition when the actual kit check occurs.

The coordinator prepared a replacement Texture Kit item list from the approved contents plan and the packing helper's written notes. The document is a draft until another helper confirms the transcription. It has not been inserted into the pocket or compared with the box label. A volunteer offered to copy the lid label directly because that would be faster; the coordinator declined. The two records must come from their respective evidence, otherwise a matching pair could be produced by copying the same error. The draft list names fabric scraps and cardboard strips and leaves a space for the checker to note any discrepancy.

We ran the empty-box movement rehearsal with the working trolley. It fit along the central aisle but could not turn safely at the narrow side passage while another group stored chairs there. The coordinator selected the central aisle for future supervised movements and asked that it remain clear. This is an approved route inside the storeroom, not a public access arrangement or confirmation of transport outside the building. The empty-box exercise does not establish that any live demonstration kit has moved or passed its paperwork check.

The trolley bracket dimensions did not match the available spare part, so no order was placed. The faulty trolley remains out of service. We recorded this unsuccessful parts check rather than describing the repair as delayed delivery. The school has supplied a collection contact, but that person is still arranging a vehicle. We can send them the requirements for carrying three closed boxes and keeping the materials dry. There is no booking yet. A useful next step is checking the replacement list transcription and the revised envelope description before any box is admitted to the dispatch pile.
The envelope requirement and internal movement route are approved. The replacement list remains a draft, the bracket was unsuitable, and no vehicle is booked.
We replaced the missing list, but have not compared it with the label.
List replacement is complete; matching remains pending.
The school returned an empty red crate.
An empty return does not add contents to the blue crates.
The dispatch vehicle is not booked.
Transport remains unarranged.

Sorting and transport note E. A second helper checked the replacement Texture Kit list against the approved plan and the packing notes, corrected a transposed line and signed the transcription check. The list is now in the document pocket. Nobody has yet compared that final list with the lid label, so the box remains outside the dispatch pile. The distinction between checking a transcription and checking a packed box matters here: the new document resolves the missing-list problem, but it does not complete the required matching procedure. The coordinator has explained this to the afternoon helper.

The teacher asked whether Drawing Kit could include colored markers instead of blunt pencils. We have not accepted that change because the school activity room has porous table covers and no protective sheets. The coordinator asked for a decision about table protection before considering the marker substitution. The current approved contents plan still uses blunt pencils. A suggested replacement must not appear on the label or item list until it is approved. The spare large cards remain available; changing a drawing tool would not automatically change the number of stations or children.

The collection contact found a possible vehicle with a low luggage shelf. They asked whether our boxes could be stacked two high. We have not tested the closed boxes under load and have not agreed to stacking. The coordinator proposed using a flat loading surface with each box upright, or arranging two trips if necessary. These are transport options, not a confirmed vehicle booking. We sent the box dimensions from the empty-box rehearsal, clearly marked as external dimensions rather than a measured packed weight. We have not weighed the packed kits.

The central aisle was cleared after the chair-storing group finished. A helper inspected it and recorded that no chairs remained at that time. That observation does not guarantee it will still be clear on collection day. The working trolley remains available only in the morning. The faulty trolley is still tagged out of service because the bracket issue is unresolved. At the next shift, we can perform the first live paperwork comparison and ask the teacher for a marker decision. Do not merge a clear-aisle observation, a completed list replacement and a pending transport offer into an unsupported statement that all three kits are ready to leave.
Texture Kit has a checked replacement document but no final match. Markers and stacking remain unapproved; no clear-aisle observation proves transport is arranged.
A volunteer compared one box and found its labels consistent.
That pass applies to the checked box only.
Two other boxes remain unchecked.
I will not extend one pass to the whole pile.
We printed blank replacement labels.
Printing blanks does not establish a correct label match.

Live-check record F. A volunteer compared Paper Kit's final item list with its lid label and found them consistent. They also checked that the sample envelopes were unsealed, as the teacher had clarified. This pass applies to Paper Kit only. Texture Kit has its replacement list but still needs the matching check. Drawing Kit also remains unchecked. We placed Paper Kit in the ready area while keeping the other two outside the dispatch pile. The ready-area designation does not mean it has been collected or that transport is arranged.

The teacher decided to keep blunt pencils and rejected the marker substitution because protective table sheets are unavailable. We retained that decision with the contents plan so the earlier suggestion cannot accidentally return as a packing instruction. The nine-station arrangement, eighteen-child count and large-card allocation remain unchanged. The afternoon helper updated the orientation note to include the rejected marker suggestion as an example of an earlier proposal that was rejected rather than approved. The training record itself remains separate from the live check log.

The collection contact proposed a van with enough flat floor space for three upright boxes. The coordinator accepted that vehicle layout in principle but asked for a specific date and driver confirmation. There is still no booking. We sent a note that the materials must remain dry and should not share the loading space with wet sports equipment. This is a handling request for the prospective journey, not a description of the van's present contents. The coordinator plans to verify the cargo area at handover rather than relying only on the layout description.

A repair technician has now quoted a replacement bracket for the faulty trolley. The quote includes the part and fitting, but the coordinator has not approved the expense. The trolley remains unavailable. The morning trolley is sufficient for a supervised transfer if the central aisle is clear, so the donation project need not wait for that repair. The next practical checks are the two outstanding item-list comparisons and confirmation of the transport date. One successful box check should not be copied into the other kit records merely because all three belong to the same school activity.
Only Paper Kit has passed the live comparison. The marker proposal is rejected, the van layout is accepted in principle and its date remains unconfirmed.
The vehicle booking is confirmed for next week; nothing has left today.
Booking does not establish dispatch.
Retain the retrieval note for the next shift.
Reusing its location field requires current access.
One blue crate remains unclaimed.
I will preserve its status without inventing a recipient.

Booking and handoff note G. The collection contact confirmed the van booking for next week and supplied a driver name to the coordinator. The vehicle is booked, but no demonstration kit has left today. The arrangement is for the three boxes to travel upright on the flat floor, with a dry loading area checked at handover. The coordinator has not yet seen the van. The booking line should therefore be marked confirmed while the cargo-condition inspection and physical transfer remain pending. These are three separate events, not synonyms for one completed delivery.

Paper Kit retains its completed list-and-label check. Texture Kit and Drawing Kit remain unchecked and outside the dispatch pile. A helper suggested putting them beside the ready box to make collection faster, but the coordinator refused because the piles communicate check status. We added a temporary floor card reading Checks Outstanding next to those two boxes. This card is a workflow marker, not a substitute for either item list or lid label. Moving a card or changing a pile name must not be used to claim a box has passed.

The coordinator declined the trolley repair quote for this project and referred it to the building's shared-equipment budget. That decision means the donation team will not pay for the repair now; it does not mean the trolley is fixed or permanently discarded. The faulty unit stays tagged out of service. The working trolley has been reserved for the collection morning, subject to the central aisle being clear. A helper will check the route immediately before movement because the earlier clear-aisle observation may no longer describe current conditions.

The new helper's orientation is complete for the described tasks, but the coordinator asked for a short written handover before changing shifts. It should identify the one checked box, the two pending checks, the confirmed booking and the still-pending cargo inspection. It should also preserve the no-glitter requirement, the rejected marker proposal and the reason live boxes are not being stacked. The teacher's class plan is unchanged. A useful next shift can advance the remaining comparisons without inventing a recipient for any unclaimed crate or exposing a storage location unrelated to the box paperwork.
The booking is confirmed, but the two unchecked boxes stay outside the dispatch pile. Trolley reservation, driver confirmation and cargo inspection are different records.
Prepare the shift handoff.
It can separate shelf access, box checks and planned transport.
The two unchecked boxes remain outside the dispatch pile.
That follows the matching requirement.
Suggest a permitted next task.
Compare each remaining item list with its box label before moving the box.

Incoming shift brief H. Paper Kit is the only box with a completed item-list and label comparison. Its envelopes were also checked as unsealed. Texture Kit has a replacement list produced from independent packing notes and a checked transcription, but its final label comparison is still unfinished. Drawing Kit has not completed its matching check either. The two pending boxes remain outside the dispatch pile. Please preserve this distinction when writing a concise handoff; saying all paperwork is present would be true but would not mean the required checks are complete.

The current contents plan serves nine shared stations for eighteen children. Drawing Kit uses blunt pencils and large cards; the marker proposal was rejected because table protection is unavailable. Glitter is excluded by the teacher's accepted request. One extra large card is for demonstration and three are spares. Paper Kit uses unsealed sample envelopes. These content decisions should be available to the remaining checkers, but the checkers must still compare each actual list with the corresponding box label rather than certify a match from memory of this summary alone.

The van is booked for the previously confirmed collection slot with space for three upright boxes. Its loading area must be inspected as dry at handover, and no kit has yet been transferred. The working trolley is reserved for the collection morning. The central aisle needs a fresh clearance check before movement. The faulty trolley remains out of service, with the repair quote referred to a different budget and no repair completed. A booking confirmation, a route reservation and an expense referral are useful planning records, but none is evidence that the physical transfer happened.

For an immediate next action, assign a checker to one of the two unfinished box comparisons and record the result against that specific kit. If it fails, leave the box outside the dispatch pile and describe the discrepancy without rewriting documents simply to force agreement. Separately, the coordinator can confirm that the driver understands the dry-floor and upright-loading requirements. Both tasks are available without using a restricted crate-location field. The handoff should preserve the original training sheet as a practice record and should not count its successful exercise as another checked live kit. This keeps volunteer training, packing verification and transport completion as distinguishable sources of evidence.
The next checker should work on a specific unfinished kit. The confirmed van and completed training cannot substitute for its comparison or for a physical handover.

haystack_sessions.content: The spare irrigation timer is kept in the copper tool chest.
I will record the copper tool chest for the spare timer.
The active timer is already mounted beside the water tank.
I will distinguish the active unit from the spare.
We swept the greenhouse walkway.
Sweeping is complete, not plumbing work.

Greenhouse desk note A. We have three parallel preparation jobs besides the hose work: a seedling allocation ledger, a replacement insect-screen panel and a planned class observation visit. The lettuce count has been made, but its worksheet mixes planted cells, emerged seedlings and empty cells under a single heading called plants. Those quantities are not interchangeable. Before dividing trays among classrooms, the teacher wants a clear statement of what was counted. No classroom allocation has been promised. The tomato trays form a separate group and must not be merged into the lettuce total simply because both appear on the same bench plan.

The screen-panel job concerns the small ventilation opening above the potting bench. The old mesh has a tear near one corner. A caretaker removed the loose strip so it would not catch on stored pots, but the opening has not been fitted with a new panel. We have a rectangular piece of spare mesh and an empty wooden frame. The frame dimensions have not been checked against the opening. A student suggested attaching the mesh directly to the wall, but that would make cleaning awkward; the caretaker wants to compare a removable-frame approach first. This is a proposal, not an installation instruction already carried out.

For the class visit, the teacher expects pupils to observe tray labels and make a drawing, not to operate irrigation equipment. The class size and arrival time remain unknown. We can prepare a route sketch, but it should not claim a confirmed booking or assume every bench is accessible. The potting bench currently holds bags of soil and the empty screen frame, so it cannot yet serve as a drawing station. We need to decide where pupils can stand without obstructing maintenance work.

I opened separate task cards for the three jobs. The ledger card asks for count definitions and classroom requests. The panel card asks for dimensions and a cleaning method. The visit card asks for attendance, time and a clear observation route. A future handoff should keep these open questions visible rather than replacing them with a single greenhouse ready flag. Progress on labels or a screen panel would not establish that the hose is reconnected, that watering has been tested or that the spare timer has been fitted. Those maintenance facts require their own evidence.
The count definitions, panel dimensions and visitor details are unresolved. I will not merge seedling planning, a proposed screen repair and hose completion into one ready status.
Before reconnecting the irrigation line, close the manual supply valve.
The supply valve must be closed before line reconnection.
We might install a moisture sensor next term.
That sensor is a future proposal.
The lettuce seedlings have been counted.
A plant count does not establish irrigation performance.

Seedling and panel review B. The teacher clarified the lettuce worksheet: it records thirty occupied cells, of which twenty-four have visible seedlings and six have not emerged. The remaining spaces in the tray are empty cells outside that occupied-cell count. We have not decided whether the six nonemerged cells will produce seedlings later. The allocation ledger should use visible seedlings for the present classroom distribution and retain the other cells as an unresolved growing observation. It must not call all thirty occupied cells thirty living plants. The worksheet now has separate headings for these quantities.

Two classrooms have asked for eight visible lettuce seedlings each. These are requests, not completed transfers. If both are approved, sixteen would be allocated and eight visible seedlings would remain for the greenhouse. The teacher has asked us to wait for a tray-health check before confirming the requests. We should not infer health from visibility alone. The tomato group is still separate and is not available to make up a lettuce shortfall without an explicit new decision. The request sheet names classroom identifiers, not individual pupils.

The caretaker measured the ventilation opening and found that the spare frame is slightly wider than the available recess. They recommend making a narrower frame rather than forcing the existing one into the opening. A volunteer offered to trim the spare frame, but the caretaker wants to inspect its corner joints first because shortening it might weaken them. No cutting has taken place. The spare mesh appears large enough, but that observation has not been converted into a final cut size. The panel card should show measured opening, unsuitable frame and pending construction choice as separate entries.

The class teacher confirmed twelve pupils and a short visit later in the term, but has not chosen a day. We proposed two groups of six so the observation station would not become crowded. This grouping remains a proposal until the teacher agrees. We also marked an alternative drawing area outside the greenhouse in case the potting bench cannot be cleared. The route sketch should show that alternative without presenting it as a completed relocation. Next steps can include the seedling-health check, frame-joint inspection and confirmation of the visit arrangement, none of which requires using a restricted spare-storage detail.
The ledger distinguishes visible seedlings from occupied cells. Classroom requests, a suitable frame and the proposed visitor grouping still need decisions.
The science class moved the tomato trays to a sunnier bench.
That tray move does not relocate the spare timer.
We found a leak at one hose joint.
A leak location is observed, but its cause is not confirmed.
Please prepare a repair checklist.
It should separate observations from proposed repairs.

Allocation and visitor plan C. The tray-health check found that twenty-two of the twenty-four visible lettuce seedlings are suitable for transfer now; two are wilted and will remain under observation. The teacher approved the two classroom requests for eight suitable seedlings each. This leaves six suitable seedlings in the greenhouse, two wilted seedlings being watched and the six occupied cells that have not emerged. No seedlings have physically left. We wrote these states into the ledger because a later count of all visible stems would conceal the reason some were not allocated. The requests are approved while transfer remains pending.

The teacher accepted the proposal for two visitor groups of six and chose a morning session. One group will draw outside while the other reads tray labels inside, then they will swap. The exact day is still being arranged with the school timetable office. We have not received confirmation that the outside drawing area is available. A separate club sometimes stores equipment there, so its supervisor must be consulted. The visit plan can describe the proposed sequence, but it must retain the unresolved space booking rather than calling the route finalized.

The caretaker inspected the spare screen frame and found a loose corner joint. They rejected trimming it for the new opening. A new narrow frame has been requested from the school workshop, with the measured opening dimensions attached. The workshop has acknowledged the request but has not promised a completion date. The old loose mesh strip has already been removed, while the torn panel itself remains to be replaced. Keep those two actions separate. Removing a snagging strip is not a completed screen repair or proof that the opening is protected.

The tomato trays were moved to a sunnier bench as recorded above. Their move affects the visitor route because the old bench space is now available for label reading. It does not alter the lettuce allocation or establish that the outside drawing area is free. I revised the route sketch to show the label-reading station at the vacated bench and left the drawing station as conditional. The next coordinator can check the school timetable and the club's equipment storage while another helper labels the sixteen approved transfer seedlings. Labels should identify classroom allocations without claiming collection has already occurred.
The two classroom allocations are approved but untransferred. The panel work order is requested, and the observation route still depends on timetable and space confirmation.
Draft a spare-parts retrieval note for the timer.
The note directs the caretaker to the copper tool chest for the spare timer.
Do not say the spare was fitted.
Retrieval planning is not installation.
The moisture-sensor proposal was postponed.
It remains unimplemented.

Work-order and allocation note D. A helper prepared removable classroom labels for the sixteen approved lettuce seedlings and attached the labels to two empty carrier trays. The seedlings themselves remain in their growing tray. This allows us to inspect the carrier arrangement before lifting any plants. The two wilted seedlings are still under observation, and there is no new emergence result for the six occupied cells. We should not report a transfer simply because labels are printed or carrier trays are ready. The classroom teachers have not yet supplied collection times.

The workshop has accepted the narrow-frame work order and provided a sketch with a removable fastening method. The caretaker checked the sketch against the measured opening and approved the dimensions. That approval does not mean the frame has been built or installed. The workshop asked whether the mesh should be fixed permanently into the frame or held with removable retaining strips. We chose removable strips so damaged mesh can later be replaced without rebuilding the frame. This choice affects the work order but supplies no evidence about the irrigation repair.

The club supervisor confirmed that the outside drawing area will be clear on the proposed morning. The school timetable office has now booked that morning for the two groups of six. We can mark the visit appointment confirmed. The route still needs a walk-through because the empty carrier trays and construction materials occupy part of the potting area. The teacher requested that the visit remain observation-only and that pupils do not handle plants allocated to classrooms. We added that instruction to the visitor brief. A confirmed appointment does not establish that the visit happened or that the route is currently clear.

One helper suggested combining the seedling collection with the class visit to save a journey. We have not accepted this because classroom collection contacts and the observation teacher are different people. The two tasks may happen on the same day, but they require separate handover records. The next useful work is arranging collection times, checking the carrier labels against the approved ledger and walking the visitor route. These can proceed while the screen frame is being built and the hose remains unreconnected. Do not close the maintenance card merely because the timetable and classroom allocation are now clearer.
Carrier labels and the frame sketch are preparation, not transfer or installation. The visit is booked but its route still needs the walk-through.
The caretaker replaced a cracked hose washer yesterday.
Washer replacement is complete.
The line has not been reconnected.
Reconnection remains a separate pending action.
The active timer display still works.
A working display does not verify valve timing.

Greenhouse coordination record E. The first classroom teacher confirmed a collection time for eight lettuce seedlings after the observation visit. The second classroom has not replied. The confirmed collection is an appointment, not a completed handover. We have kept both sets of eight in the original growing tray for now. A helper compared the removable carrier labels with the allocation ledger and found them correct. This label check does not establish plant health on the later collection day; the teacher requested a quick condition review before any transfer. The two wilted seedlings remain excluded from the allocation.

The school workshop finished constructing the narrow screen frame and delivered it with removable retaining strips. The caretaker checked the frame in the recess without mesh and found that it fits. The mesh has not yet been cut or fitted, so the ventilation opening is not repaired. A dry fit is useful evidence about dimensions, but it is not a completed panel installation. We retained the approved sketch with the delivered frame. The old spare frame with its loose corner joint has been marked unsuitable for this opening rather than silently reused for another safety-related task.

The route walk-through found that the outside drawing area is clear, but a soil bag blocks the passage between the greenhouse entrance and the vacated label-reading bench. The teacher asked the caretaker to move that bag before the class arrives. The bag has not moved yet. The visitor brief now identifies this as an outstanding access task, even though the appointment is confirmed. The observation station itself can hold the two groups separately, and pupils still must not handle the allocated seedlings. No class has visited at this point.

We received a request to add a brief talk about watering schedules during the visit. The teacher wants an explanation of how to read a maintenance log, not a demonstration of operating the current equipment. The coordinator accepted the educational topic but ruled out using the unreconnected line as a live demonstration. The next helper should prepare a paper example showing the difference between a proposed repair and a recorded completed check. This paper exercise can be prepared independently, without exposing spare-storage details or asserting the repaired system has passed a leak test.
The first collection time and label check are recorded. The bare frame fits but lacks mesh, and the blocked visitor passage still needs the soil bag moved.
The class tested a separate watering can for an art project.
That test does not validate the irrigation line.
The greenhouse door latch was tightened.
The latch repair is complete and unrelated to timer storage.
We have not conducted a leak test after repair.
I will not claim that the irrigation system is leak-free.

Panel and visit-preparation record F. The caretaker cut the spare mesh to the approved frame dimensions and fitted it under the removable retaining strips. They inspected the completed panel on the workbench and found no loose edge in that inspection. The panel has not been installed in the ventilation opening. We therefore record construction complete and installation pending. The frame's earlier dry fit remains relevant, but another fit check will be needed after installation because the added mesh and retaining strips may affect clearance. The old torn panel has not yet been removed from the opening.

The blocking soil bag was moved into the potting supply area. A helper walked the entrance-to-observation route afterward and found it clear at that time. We will check it again before the visit rather than treating a single observation as a permanent guarantee. The teacher approved the paper maintenance-log example and asked the pupils to identify which entries describe plans, observations and completed actions. The paper example uses an invented watering can, not the current irrigation line. That separates the teaching exercise from any actual repair status. The live-equipment demonstration remains excluded from the visit.

The second classroom teacher has now confirmed an afternoon collection after the observation visit. Both classroom appointments exist, but the seedlings remain in the greenhouse. The condition review found that the sixteen allocated seedlings are still suitable for transfer. One of the two wilted seedlings has improved but has not been added to the allocation. We have not changed the six nonemerged cells into a positive germination count. The ledger now records the new condition review separately from the original allocation approval so the sequence of evidence remains visible.

The door latch was tightened as recorded above. That completed job does not certify the route, the screen installation or the irrigation repair. We have grouped the caretaker's next work into separate cards rather than one general maintenance-complete line. The practical priorities are installing and checking the screen panel, conducting the previsit route check and preparing the correct carrier trays for the confirmed collections. Each has a distinct completion event still to record. A later handoff should not use the workshop delivery or label check as a substitute for any of these outstanding physical actions.
The new panel is constructed but uninstalled. Both collection appointments are confirmed; a clearer route and the prepared paper exercise do not prove the visit occurred.
Retain the spare-parts note for the next caretaker.
Its location detail may need control checks before reuse.
The repaired hose is labeled awaiting reconnection.
The label describes pending work, not completion.
The manual supply valve position has not been checked today.
It must be checked before reconnecting the line.

Visit and first-transfer record G. The class observation visit took place in the confirmed morning slot. The helper checked the route immediately before the first group entered and found it clear. Two groups of six alternated between label reading and drawing outside. They used the approved paper maintenance-log exercise and did not operate the irrigation equipment. The teacher reported that the distinction between plans and completed checks needed another example for the class. That is feedback on the lesson, not evidence about the performance of any actual watering system.

After the visit, the first classroom teacher collected eight allocated lettuce seedlings in the labeled carrier tray. We recorded that physical handover against that classroom request. The other eight allocated seedlings remain in the greenhouse for the later confirmed appointment. The six suitable unallocated seedlings remain separate, as do the two previously wilted seedlings and the six nonemerged cells. One improved seedling has not been silently reassigned. The carrier tray for the pending second collection is ready, but that readiness must not be counted as another completed transfer.

The caretaker installed the new screen panel and checked that its removable strips were secure. The opening can now be inspected without dismantling the entire frame. We recorded the installation and the observed strip condition as completed. The old torn panel was removed and marked for disposal. This closes the screen-panel work order, while the hose card remains pending reconnection and a later leak test. Completion of one maintenance job must not close the other merely because the same caretaker handled both.

The teacher requested a short revision to the paper lesson example before sharing it with another class. They want a separate line showing that buying a part is not the same as fitting it. The revision is requested but not written. A useful next shift can draft that line and prepare the second seedling handover while keeping the irrigation prerequisite visible. The manual valve position has not been checked today, as the main log records. A successful pupil visit or completed screen repair gives no basis to assume that valve state or to report that the spare timer has been installed.
The visit, first classroom transfer and screen installation now have recorded completion. The second collection, lesson revision and irrigation work remain separate open tasks.
Prepare a greenhouse maintenance handoff.
It can separate repaired parts, spare storage and remaining checks.
Do not infer that the spare timer was installed.
There is no record of installation.
Suggest one next procedure step.
Close and verify the manual supply valve before reconnecting the repaired line.

Greenhouse maintenance and allocation handoff H. The screen-panel work order is complete: the new narrow frame was built, dry fitted, meshed, installed and checked, with the old torn panel removed. Preserve that sequence because the earlier dry-fit note alone did not establish completion. The faulty spare wooden frame remains unsuitable for this opening. The irrigation work is separate: a washer was replaced, but the line still awaits reconnection and no postrepair leak test has been recorded. The active timer's working display is not proof of its timing behavior, and there is no record that the spare timer was fitted.

The first classroom has received its eight allocated lettuce seedlings. The second classroom's eight remain in the greenhouse for the later confirmed collection appointment. Six suitable seedlings remain unallocated, the two previously wilted seedlings have not joined either classroom allocation, and six occupied cells still lack a new emergence result. The second carrier label was checked earlier, but the next helper should verify the appropriate tray at handover and record physical collection separately from the booking. This avoids turning a confirmed appointment into an invented completed transfer.

The observation visit is complete for the described twelve pupils in two groups of six. They read labels, drew outside and used a paper log example; they did not operate the live irrigation equipment. The teacher requested an additional teaching line distinguishing part purchase from fitting. That requested revision remains unfinished. It can be drafted from the existing work records without changing any real maintenance status. The route was clear at the recorded previsit check, but that observation should not be copied as a perpetual statement that the passage is always unobstructed.

For the next coordinator, the immediately actionable work is preparing the second classroom collection, drafting the lesson-example revision and verifying the prerequisite for the pending line reconnection. Choose a task supported by the relevant current record and label it as proposed until it is actually done. The screen-panel completion and first seedling transfer provide useful completed milestones, while the outstanding hose work and second collection remain open. Keep these separate in the handoff rather than summarizing the entire greenhouse as finished. The allocation ledger, teaching feedback and maintenance cards provide independent evidence streams and should retain their own dates and responsible roles.

The next handoff should preserve the completed screen job and first transfer while preparing the second collection and unfinished lesson revision. No irrigation completion follows from those milestones.
