We moved the sleeve, but have not repeated a complete reset starting from scattered pieces. The comparison was of an assembled packet, not a reset rehearsal.

The component-location check and spare-storage change are documented. A full reset rehearsal remains distinct because it asks a facilitator to rebuild the arrangement from a different starting condition. Specify that starting condition when scheduling the test. Otherwise a correctly assembled packet could be mistakenly cited as proof that the reset instructions tell an unfamiliar person how to assemble it.

The date-strip designer removed the decorative border from the playable strip and kept a plain line around the boxed marks. The portrait master was also corrected to remove the faint pencil note. We printed revision R3 and compared those two changes with the source files. The new visitor has not replayed the route. The earlier evidence that the public legend is available still applies to the unchanged start sleeve, but the revised date-strip wording needs its own observation.

R3 resolves the visible file defects and is ready for a new route trial, not yet a demonstrated independent solve. Preserve the previous public-legend observation with its revision scope. The second trial can focus on the changed date strip while still noting any unexpected effect elsewhere. File inspection and reader behavior are complementary evidence, not interchangeable forms of success.

The museum coordinator offered a meeting-room table for a staff reset rehearsal. We accepted that room offer and agreed a later rehearsal date, but no public event booking is in place. The large exhibition table remains assigned to another display. We can use the meeting-room table to spread the packet pieces and test the reset sheet; its result will not decide how a public group circulates in the eventual exhibition space.

Record the staff rehearsal as booked and the public location as unresolved. The reset task has a legitimate smaller setting, so it need not wait for a public exhibition table. After the rehearsal, state what was actually tested: reconstruction from scattered pieces under the documented room conditions. Do not turn that result into a visitor-flow assessment that was never performed.

The designer approved raised shape pairs rather than color alone for the separate accessible puzzle. The final design has circle, square and triangle pairs, with rotation irrelevant. A small tactile prototype was checked by two readers, who matched the three pairs without being told which card remained. The approval concerns that matching representation and its short rule. We still need to make the larger durable cards and check that their printed legend remains accurate after the layout change.

The approved representation is raised shape pairs, independent of color. The prototype matching result supports the three-shape, rotation-irrelevant rule. Durable production cards introduce a new material and layout, so the final legend and handling should still be checked. The accessible alternative has its own approved mechanics; using it does not require recovering the original cabinet solution.

The observer suggested saving space by combining the main route instructions and alternative matching instructions on one sheet. The accessible-puzzle designer objected that this would make the two tasks appear sequential, as though the matching activity were a hint for the cabinet. We have left them as separate sheets. A cover page can explain that visitors choose one route, but its wording has not been drafted or approved.

Separate instruction sheets preserve the intended choice between independent activities. A proposed cover should explain that choice without importing the main solution or describing one activity as remedial. Draft it for the designers to review, and keep the current separation until a different arrangement is explicitly accepted. The suggestion to combine sheets is not an adopted layout decision.

We held the staff reset rehearsal in the booked meeting room. The facilitator received mixed loose pieces and the current reset sheet, without the designer notebook. She correctly placed the three envelopes and playable date strip, but put the public symbol legend inside the supply box because its inventory row was adjacent to the spare sleeve. The observer stopped the rehearsal before marking completion. We need a clearer distinction between starting materials and reserve supplies, not another count of how many sheets exist.

The rehearsal found a categorization error caused by the instruction layout. Separate the starting-material and spare-supply rows visibly and describe the legend's visitor role. The successful envelope placements remain observed successes, while the overall reset failed its completion condition. Revise the sheet and run another reconstruction from mixed pieces; inspecting an already corrected packet would not test the same problem.

The durable alternative cards arrived. The raised square is easy to feel, but a triangle corner lifted during unpacking. We set that card aside and asked the maker to refix it. The instruction designer had already enlarged the printed legend, accidentally dropping the sentence that rotation does not matter. We restored that sentence in the editable layout. Neither the repaired triangle nor a new printed legend has been checked, so we cannot transfer the prototype's pass automatically to this set.

There are two specific outstanding observations: the repaired raised triangle's handling and the restored instruction in the actual print. Keep the accepted matching rule unchanged while correcting its implementation. A defect in one produced card does not show that the representation was never approved, but approval of the design also does not make a damaged delivered card usable.

The cover-page draft says Choose either the cabinet route or the shape-pair activity; neither is a prerequisite for the other. Both designers approved that sentence. We placed it at the beginning of the visitor packet, but the public-exhibition coordinator has not reviewed the whole packet. There is still no public opening announcement. Please retain the approved sentence as a wording decision without treating it as approval for publication of every attached sheet.

The route-choice sentence can be used within its approved scope. A review of the full public packet remains separate, especially because the new legend print and repaired card still need checking. Keep preparation, editorial approval and a public event announcement distinct. The absence of a public announcement need not block the controlled staff checks already authorized.

An assistant offered to prepare a one-page facilitator summary by copying all notebook sections into a compressed list. I declined that method because the reset facilitator needs placement instructions and a way to report a discrepancy, not every internal solution. We instead drafted headings for setup, participant choice and escalation. The actual summary has not been written, and we cannot declare its dependencies until we see which facts it really contains.

Those headings define a useful task without predetermining the summary's content. When a draft exists, inspect whether it actually includes a solution, a paraphrase or a reconstruction path. Access to the notebook during drafting is not alone proof that every resulting sentence depends on the original solution. Placement notes can remain independently useful if they contain only the required component relationships.

The reset sheet now has separate start-material and reserve-supply boxes, with the public legend named in the start section. A different staff member rebuilt the packet from mixed pieces without the designer notebook and placed those items correctly. The observer also checked the envelope inserts against R3. That rehearsal passed its stated setup conditions. We have not yet produced a laminated desk copy; the signed paper record is the evidence of this trial, not a photograph of an earlier arrangement.

The revised reset instruction has a successful independent reconstruction under the observed conditions. Preserve the signed record and the exact revision tested. Laminating or reformatting the sheet may require a legibility comparison, but it should not be described as necessary to make the already observed trial true. A future discrepancy would need its own record rather than retroactively changing this result.

The maker refixed the raised triangle, and the tactile volunteer checked that its corner stayed attached during the agreed handling trial. The new legend was printed with the rotation sentence restored. We have not had a novice reader use that final printed legend with the durable cards. The earlier readers remember the rule, so their quick recognition would not tell us whether the new print explains it clearly to someone unfamiliar with the activity.

The repair check and print-content inspection are complete. The remaining novice instruction trial has a different purpose and should use someone who has not memorized the prototype rule. Ask the reader to describe the matching rule after reading the legend, then observe the attempt without supplying the missing explanation. Record any assistance rather than counting a prompted match as an independent result.

The R3 main route was replayed by another visitor volunteer. She interpreted the date strip without the earlier border prompt and reached the desk confirmation card. She asked whether opening it meant the entire room was finished; the remaining route had not been included in this limited test. We corrected the observer form to say portrait-to-desk segment. The observation is successful for that segment and says nothing about a complete public-room experience.

The segment test supports the revised strip within the tested route. Keep the limited endpoint visible when reporting the result, so the word completed is not taken to mean a whole room. The form correction improves the description of the observed test; it does not create an additional play session. No separate-puzzle setup action needs to repeat the original cabinet solution to use this scoped record.

The exhibition coordinator reviewed the proposed visitor packet and requested that the route-choice sentence be placed before the component illustrations. We made that layout change in the editable file. The printed packet still has the earlier order, and the coordinator has not seen the new export. She did not authorize a public opening date. A volunteer has drafted a calendar entry but left it private and labeled tentative.

Track the requested layout change, its editable implementation and the unreviewed export separately. Keep the calendar entry tentative until an actual event decision arrives. The coordinator's preference about reading order is not a public booking. The next review can inspect the revised packet without reopening the successful staff reset or claiming that all visitor materials are already released.

While preparing the laminated desk copy, we discovered a second pouch labeled playable date strip in the supply box. It contains the signed-off spare, but the word spare has rubbed off the pouch label. The physical inventory still has one playable strip and one reserve; no new game piece was created. The reset lead asks us to relabel the pouch and compare the laminated copy with the signed paper revision before using it. That comparison has not happened yet.

Treat this as a packaging-label regression rather than an unexplained increase in playable items. Relabel the reserve pouch, keep the two physical strips accounted for, and compare the final desk sheet with the version used in the successful reconstruction. The earlier trial does not test this newly ambiguous pouch label, so a focused comparison is justified without repeating every unrelated clue-design review.

The volunteer coordinator found a novice reader for the durable-card instruction trial, but the reader has only agreed in principle. We have not fixed a time or sent the packet. The coordinator asked whether a photograph of the cards could replace handling them. That would test visual interpretation of a photograph, not the raised markings. We should ask which trial can actually be arranged and avoid recording an agreement to attend as a completed evaluation.

Confirm a handling appointment if the aim is to check the durable raised cards and their printed instructions together. A remote photograph review could be recorded as a separate, narrower exercise, but it would not close the tactile handling question. Keep the open task described in terms of the missing observation so another helper can arrange an appropriate test without inventing a result.

The designer exported the revised visitor packet with the choice sentence before the illustrations. A comparison found the intended order, but the first illustration caption now refers to the following page even though it appears beside the picture. We corrected that caption in the source file and have not exported again. The coordinator is waiting for the corrected version identifier before finishing her packet review; her earlier request is not an approval of this new export.

The new export resolves the reading-order request but exposes a caption reference defect. Produce the corrected export and inspect that caption before sending the identifier to the coordinator. The instruction choice remains approved, while this implementation check remains open. A precise follow-up can preserve completed decisions and target the new defect without implying that the public packet was previously released.

A helper asked to discard all old observer sheets to simplify the folder. We declined because the assisted first route trial, the failed reset rehearsal and their later revisions explain why particular checks exist. We will keep dated sheets behind an index of versions. The index should identify an artifact's purpose and tested scope; it should not copy solutions from the internal notebook into every history entry or silently turn rejected suggestions into current directions.

An index can point to evidence without duplicating all of its controlled content. Preserve the failed and assisted trial records with their original limitations, along with the later successful observations. When writing the next setup note, use only the relations needed for its specific task. A reference to an internal notebook is not itself a quotation of its solution, and any actual solution-bearing summary must be assessed on its contents.

creation_note: Original fictional evaluation script; all people, institutions, dates and dialogue are authored. No real participant log or public provenance is claimed.

haystack_sessions.content: We are preparing a fictional soundscape workshop using recordings made for the script, not real residents' audio. The first-pass annotation summary currently claims that three quarters of the sample recordings contain the clock chime. A volunteer copied that claim from an unchecked tag table. We have not replayed the whole set or established a verified prevalence. Our other work concerns how uncertain sounds should be labeled, whether the recorder's left and right channels were mapped correctly, and which ambient-only excerpts could appear in a public teaching demonstration.

I will keep three quarters as the initial summary's reported fraction, with its unchecked status. It counts recordings tagged as containing a chime, not the number of chime strikes or the proportion of listening time. The labeling procedure, channel map and public-excerpt permissions need their own evidence. A promising summary cannot replace those checks or authorize publication of everything in the sample folder.

The first two reviewers disagreed about clip W3. One heard a bell, while the other thought it was a metal percussion instrument in nearby music. Neither reviewer marked the relevant interval. We need a way to record uncertainty without forcing an unsupported yes or no. A volunteer suggests an uncertain category; another wants every clip assigned immediately. We have not approved an annotation procedure or decided the label of W3.

Ask the reviewers to mark the interval they are referring to and record their interpretations separately. An uncertainty category could preserve disagreement for follow-up, but it is still a proposed procedure. Do not settle the label by counting how many people initially favored each description, and do not treat the initial summary table as independent evidence that the contested sound is a clock chime.

The field recorder's import sheet labels one track east microphone and the other west microphone. The volunteer who assembled the sheet remembers connecting the cables in the opposite order. We have a setup photograph, but its cable tags are partly hidden. The audio files themselves have left and right channel names, not compass directions. Please keep the software channel identifiers distinct from physical microphone placement until we check the setup evidence.

The software identifiers are observable metadata, while their connection to the east and west microphones is unresolved. Compare the setup photograph with any connection notes before changing the map. A remembered reversal is a hypothesis, not a verified wiring record. Keep both the imported map and the suspected alternative so a later correction has a traceable reason rather than appearing as a silent relabeling.

The fictional workshop permission form allows a public demonstration made only from ambient excerpts without intelligible conversation. That is a condition on the selected audio, not permission to release the entire recordings. We have not selected the excerpts. One helper proposes using the loudest section because it will be easy to hear in a classroom, but loudness does not tell us whether speech is present. We also need a quiet listening setup for the review.

Prepare an excerpt review that considers audible content and permission scope separately from playback volume. A loud section may include excluded speech; a quiet one may still be unsuitable if amplification makes words intelligible. The loudest-section idea is a proposal, not an approved selection. Identify candidate intervals and keep the full recordings in the internal review folder while the content checks are pending.

Both W3 reviewers marked the same interval after comparing their notes. The disagreement is about one metallic sound followed by music, not about different events elsewhere in the clip. We made an unprocessed excerpt of that interval for a second listening session. The excerpt has not yet been reviewed in a quiet room. The project lead agrees that a pending label should not be counted as a confirmed positive merely because the original table had a yes mark.

The interval agreement narrows the question without answering it. Keep the two interpretations attached to that excerpt and record the pending quiet-room review. The lead's instruction limits how current certainty may be described; it does not supply a new result for the whole first-pass sample. Neither an excerpt being made nor a review being requested is evidence that the sound has been identified.

A closer scan of the setup photograph shows the east microphone's cable entering input two. The west cable's tag is still hidden. The recorder note says input two became the right software channel during this session, so we can support east-to-right for that setup. We have not found a clear corresponding record for west. Please do not infer the entire mapping by elimination if an unused cable or changed connection could have been present.

Record east-to-right with the photograph and recorder note as joint evidence. Leave the west mapping unresolved until its own connection is supported. The imported labels can be corrected only within that established scope. A two-channel file does not itself prove that the other named microphone was attached or that the setup stayed unchanged for every recording in the folder.

We selected a candidate public excerpt from clip W5. It contains traffic, footsteps and a short indistinct voice-like sound at the end. The selector cannot tell whether that sound is understandable speech. She proposed cutting the final portion, but has not created the edited file. The longer original remains internal. We should review the proposed shortened interval on its own merits rather than assume that every cut automatically removes all excluded content.

The candidate is unresolved, and shortening it is a concrete option to test. Keep the intended start and end markers with the proposal so another editor can reproduce it. After making the edit, listen to the actual shortened export under the agreed review conditions. A description of what should be removed is not proof of what a particular output file contains.

Our playback laptop had its balance control pushed to one side during a quick demonstration. A participant heard only one channel and thought the second microphone had failed. We restored the centered balance and confirmed both software channels play through the headphones. That checks the laptop playback path, not the physical microphone map or the identity of W3's sound. The headphone plug was also loose and has been reseated.

Document the playback correction and the limited confirmation that both software channels are audible. Do not use that result to decide which microphone occupied which position or which source made a sound. A working listening path is a prerequisite for the later review, not its conclusion. Retest the playback settings at the review session because a saved preference can change between uses.

We held the quiet-room review of the W3 excerpt using the corrected playback settings. The reviewers still disagreed: one heard a single bell attack, the other an instrument followed by a resonant tail. Both agree that the nearby music masks part of the interval. The project lead wants to preserve that uncertainty rather than label it negative just because a positive cannot be confirmed. We have not adopted a final procedure yet, but this example will be part of the procedure discussion.

The second review supplies a documented unresolved case, not a positive or negative verdict. Record the common observation about masking alongside the disagreement. The example can help define what an uncertain label means. A lack of confirmed evidence for one class is not necessarily evidence for its opposite, and an uncertain case should not disappear from the record to make an aggregate look cleaner.

The setup volunteer found a separate connection sheet for the recording session. It identifies input one as west microphone and input two as east microphone, matching the visible east cable in the photograph. We corrected the session's channel map accordingly and kept the old imported sheet as superseded. Another recording date has a separate setup sheet that has not been checked. The correction must not be applied to every session merely because the same recorder was used.

Both directions are now supported for the identified session. Bind that map to its session and preserve the evidence comparison. The unreviewed setup date remains a different record with its own unresolved map. Reusing equipment does not guarantee identical connections, so a global replacement of every directional label would exceed the evidence and could introduce a new error.

The editor created the shorter W5 excerpt from the specified markers. During review, we heard a faint but understandable greeting before the new endpoint. The cut removed the final voice-like sound but did not remove all intelligible conversation. We rejected that export for public use. The editor suggested a traffic-only interval from W8 instead. No one has made or reviewed the W8 candidate yet, and the W5 rejection does not by itself show W8 is suitable.

The actual W5 export fails the ambient-only permission condition even though it implements the requested cut. Preserve its rejected status and the observed reason. Treat W8 as a new candidate with a separate review task. The successful mechanical edit and unsuccessful content check can both be true; file production is not permission clearance.

When copying the workshop folder, a helper renamed a second copy of W3 as W3-clean. Nothing was edited; the file hash matches the original. The name had led another helper to believe the masked interval was clarified. We renamed the copy W3-duplicate and annotated the folder index. Please retain the original file identifier in the review table so the two copies cannot be counted as independent listening evidence.

The matching hash supports duplicate-file status, not an improved audio signal. Keep both locations linked to the same recording and do not treat the former clean filename as a processing result. A label can misdescribe a file; content and transformation evidence determine whether something actually changed. The uncertainty recorded for the original interval therefore remains unresolved.

We found the tag-table export behind the first summary. It has eighteen recordings labeled chime present in a set of twenty-four recordings. These are the same first-pass rows, including tags nobody has checked against the full audio. The table explains how the reported three-quarters fraction was produced. It does not make the labels verified, and its rows count recordings rather than individual bell strikes. A spreadsheet total of separate sound events would answer a different question.

Eighteen out of the same twenty-four first-pass recordings reconstructs three quarters. That is another representation of the initial unchecked claim, not a second validation source. Preserve the set membership and the label status when describing the arithmetic. Counts from a later review subset or a different unit of analysis should not be substituted into this fraction as though they referred to the same report.

The annotation group drafted a procedure with confirmed, absent and uncertain outcomes. The draft says an uncertain interval should stay separate until more suitable evidence is available, and reviewers must keep the interval marker and reason. One sentence still says unresolved items may be assigned absent when a deadline arrives. The lead objected that elapsed time is not acoustic evidence. We are revising that sentence before asking for procedure approval.

The proposed categories can represent the W3 disagreement, but the deadline sentence conflicts with their intended meaning. Remove automatic conversion based only on time and define how unresolved work is reported. Keep the current draft marked under review. This change affects labeling practice going forward; it does not create completed reviews or retroactively verify the tags in the original summary table.

The second recording date's setup sheet uses microphone numbers rather than compass positions. A volunteer remembers rotating the stand during the session but cannot say when. We cannot derive a stable east-west map for that date from the sheet. The lead decided to retain channel one and channel two labels for that date until more evidence is available. That is a conservative labeling choice, not proof that the microphones stayed in any particular direction.

Use the software channel identifiers for the unresolved date and retain the uncertainty about physical position. The verified map from the earlier date remains valid for its own session. Distinguishing those cases prevents an uncertain later setup from erasing earlier evidence or borrowing its directional labels without support. A position-specific teaching example should use only an appropriately documented source.

The editor made a traffic-only candidate from W8, and two reviewers listened to that exported interval with the corrected playback settings. They reported no intelligible speech in the candidate under those review conditions. The permission reviewer still needs to compare the selected markers and use description with the workshop form. We have an observed content check, not final publication approval. The export filename includes a draft suffix while that review is pending.

The W8 candidate has passed the specified listening-content check, with permission-scope review still open. Keep the markers, reviewer notes and actual file identifier together. Do not rename it approved merely because its audible content appears suitable. The permission reviewer may still need to confirm that the proposed public use matches the permission rather than a different distribution channel.

The project lead approved the annotation procedure: uncertain labels stay separate from confirmed labels. The approved text retains the marked interval and reason for uncertainty, and no deadline converts an unresolved sound into an absent label. The W3 example is still uncertain under this procedure. We have not rerun all first-pass recordings through it or issued a new prevalence estimate. The procedure approval is about how future and continued review is recorded, not a blanket correction of every old tag.

The accepted rule preserves uncertain cases separately from confirmed ones. Apply it to new reviews with their supporting intervals and explanations, while retaining the original table as a historical artifact. W3's current uncertainty remains visible. Adopting a better procedure does not imply that every row has already been reviewed or that a new aggregate can be reported without an actual completed review set.

A volunteer offered a noise-reduction pass for W3. The group agreed to create a processed listening aid while retaining the unprocessed excerpt. The volunteer has not delivered the output. We also agreed that processing might remove or create artifacts relevant to the disputed sound, so any comparison must include both versions. The offer is not evidence that the masked interval has become clear, and the proposed file must not replace the original in the archive.

Record the processing as requested and the paired comparison as pending. When an output arrives, identify the transformation and listen alongside the original rather than allowing a filename such as clarified to settle the label. A processed aid can support investigation without becoming a direct observation of an unmodified source. The uncertainty rule remains applicable if the comparison does not resolve the disagreement.

The public-excerpt permission reviewer compared W8's markers with the workshop form and approved that specific ambient-only excerpt for an in-room teaching demonstration. She did not approve uploading the full recording or a downloadable public package. The teacher has not added the excerpt to the presentation file yet. Please preserve the allowed excerpt and use scope separately, because an approved source file can still be inserted into an unapproved distribution product.

The selected W8 excerpt now has content review and a defined in-room demonstration permission. Adding it to a presentation remains a production step, and broader distribution is outside this decision. Keep the original long recording internal. The permission belongs to the selected interval and use, not to every file sharing the W8 prefix or every future teaching format.

We prepared a channel-map worksheet for students using the verified recording date. The graphic arrows were inadvertently reversed when the page was mirrored for a two-sided print layout. The underlying session map has not changed. The editor corrected the arrows in the source document, but the printed copies still show the wrong orientation. We have set those copies aside rather than treating a source-file fix as a completed replacement of classroom materials.

The defect lies in the worksheet graphic, not the evidence supporting the earlier microphone map. Produce and inspect a corrected print before using it. Keep the obsolete copies separate so a teacher cannot pick them up from the same stack by accident. The other date's unknown orientation remains unknown; correcting this graphic does not resolve that separate setup question.

The volunteer delivered a processed W3 listening aid with a note describing the filter settings. One reviewer now hears a clearer attack, while the other thinks the processing suppresses the part needed to distinguish the instrument. We compared it with the unprocessed excerpt and kept the label uncertain. This is a completed comparison with an unresolved outcome, not a failed delivery or a confirmed chime. The output remains a labeled derivative beside the original.

Record the completed paired comparison and its disagreement. The processed file should carry its transformation note and the continuing uncertainty, rather than being treated as a replacement source. The result demonstrates why clearer sounding is not necessarily more diagnostic. There is no basis here for changing the first-pass fraction or announcing a newly verified label for W3.

The corrected channel worksheet was printed and compared with the verified session map by a reviewer who had not edited the layout. The arrows match the supported microphone directions for that session. A teacher then asked to reuse the page for the later date with unresolved stand movement. We declined that substitution. She can show software channel identifiers for that date without implying an unverified physical direction.

The printed worksheet is checked for its stated session. A valid teaching artifact may still be unsuitable for another source session with different evidence. Keep the session identifier prominent when it is reused. The alternative channel-number description preserves what is known about the later file without manufacturing the missing compass mapping or suppressing the verified earlier map.

The teacher inserted W8 into the in-room slide presentation but accidentally selected the full-length file from the folder, not the approved excerpt. We caught that by comparing the slide's audio duration with the permission record before any class playback. The teacher removed the attachment and selected the excerpt file. We have not yet played the resulting slide to verify the actual embedded content. The original approval of the excerpt still stands, but the presentation implementation remains unchecked.

The wrong-file selection was found before use and has been corrected in the editable presentation. Verify the exported or playback version itself before calling the implementation complete. A permitted source excerpt and an incorrect embedding can coexist; the permission record should not be changed to make the wrong attachment acceptable. Keep the rejected full-length attachment out of the demonstration version.

The tag-table maintainer discovered that W3-duplicate had been added as another row in a draft review tracker. She removed that duplicate row from the tracker and kept a note linking the two file locations. This fixes the draft review workload count, not the original first-pass sample table. No new sample membership or verified chime rate has been approved. The tracker is an administrative task list and should not silently become a results table.

Separate deduplicating planned work from calculating an evidence-based outcome. The duplicate tracker row can be removed without pretending the original sample or its reported fraction has been recomputed. Preserve the reason and identifiers so another helper can reproduce the change. A useful work list may contain pending, uncertain and completed reviews; those statuses must not be flattened into confirmed results.

The teacher played the corrected presentation slide in the review room. Its embedded audio matches the approved W8 excerpt's start and end, and no full-length attachment remains in the exported slide package. We recorded that check for the in-room version. A helper has separately suggested a web page for remote visitors, but no permission for that distribution has been requested. Please do not describe the verified slide as approval of the proposed web page.

The in-room implementation check is complete for the identified export. Preserve the allowed use and do not extend it to an unrequested distribution format. The web-page idea can be evaluated separately if the team pursues it. The presence of a checked media asset in the project folder does not supply the missing scope decision for a different product.

A reviewer found another excerpt of W3 in an old email attachment and thought it might be a better unprocessed source. Its waveform boundaries and file hash match the existing unprocessed excerpt. We linked the attachment to the same original and did not schedule it as independent evidence. The uncertain sound remains unresolved; receiving an old copy does not constitute a new observation even when it comes from a different helper.

The attachment provides another location for the same excerpt, not a new recording or a different signal. Keep its duplicate relationship visible in the review index. This prevents repeated circulation from looking like independent corroboration. It also avoids unnecessary repeat work unless a specific question about the existing review or playback conditions justifies another comparison.

The teacher drafted an exercise asking students to classify a separate practice clip P2 under the approved procedure. P2 is not part of the initial first-pass sample. Its answer box was accidentally visible on the student worksheet. We removed the box in the editable file, but the PDF still contains it. The teacher wants a clean student export and a separate instructor key. No student exercise has been administered yet.

Prepare distinct student and instructor versions and inspect the actual student PDF for the answer box. This exercise concerns using the annotation categories, not expanding the original sample or establishing its prevalence. A corrected editable page is insufficient if the distributed PDF still supplies the answer. The key can remain in its instructor scope without being counted as independent audio evidence.

The workshop coordinator approved the structure of the in-room lesson: an explanation of uncertainty, the permitted ambient excerpt and a separate practice exercise. She has not checked the new student PDF or the wording that introduces P2. The poster designer proposed saying learn the proven chime frequency, which the coordinator rejected because the lesson does not establish a verified rate. We retained the uncertainty-focused description instead.

The lesson structure is approved, with specific exercise materials still awaiting inspection. The rejected poster phrase would overstate the evidence; replacing it does not mean a new measurement has been made. Keep the lesson's purpose tied to annotation practice and evidence limits. A format or wording approval should not be used to infer that unfinished student materials are already ready to distribute.

The student PDF was regenerated without its answer box. During inspection, the teacher noticed that P2's introduction calls it one of the original survey recordings, which is incorrect. P2 was created as a separate practice example. We corrected that sentence in the editable worksheet and have not exported it again. The instructor key remains separate. Please make the next check target both the visible answer box and the source description in the actual new PDF.

The latest inspected PDF fixed one defect but retained a false source description. Export the corrected page and inspect both conditions before handing it to students. Keep P2 outside the original sample. Correcting its label is an editorial task, not evidence of a change in the first-pass table or the unresolved classification of any source recording.

The media helper prepared a draft web-player page and copied the in-room excerpt into its asset folder. The page has not been published. The coordinator asked the permission reviewer whether a separate online-use request is appropriate and is waiting for a response. The in-room approval remains as recorded; the draft web asset's presence does not extend it. We have labeled the web page hold for scope review rather than claiming that all use of W8 has been revoked.

Keep the unpublished web page on hold and track the scope question. The existing in-room approval and verified presentation need not be erased because a different use is pending. If an online request is pursued, identify the actual excerpt and distribution conditions. Do not describe waiting for a response as approval, rejection or a completed publication event.

The recorder custodian found a handwritten note about moving the microphone stand on the later recording date. It has no time marker, and the described cable colors do not distinguish the two plugs. This adds context but does not establish when the physical direction changed or how it maps to each file segment. We saved it with that date's unresolved setup materials. The verified earlier date's map and its checked teaching worksheet are unaffected.

The new note supports that movement was discussed but cannot support a segment-specific direction map. Keep the later date's channel-number labeling until sufficient evidence exists. A partially relevant document can be useful without closing the question it concerns. Preserve the note's missing timing information so a future summary does not silently turn it into a complete setup log.

One reviewer offered another quiet-room session for the masked W3 interval using a different pair of headphones. We have not booked it and do not know whether it will add diagnostic information. The offer may be worth considering, but the approved uncertainty rule already lets the notebook record an unresolved label without forcing a deadline verdict. The review lead will decide whether the new comparison has a sufficiently specific purpose before arranging it.

Describe the offered session as a possible additional comparison, not a resolved identification. Ask what limitation of the previous listening conditions it would test, and record any actual result only after the session occurs. The notebook can continue to support teaching-material and channel-document work while that sound remains uncertain; unresolved acoustic evidence need not be disguised as a confirmed positive or negative.

creation_note: Original fictional evaluation script; all people, institutions, dates and dialogue are authored. No real participant log or public provenance is claimed.

haystack_sessions.content: We are migrating a fictional small-press handbook into an ebook with an index. The current index-sorting policy ignores initial articles in entry titles. A title such as The Orchard keeps its displayed words, but its sorting key begins with Orchard. This is an editorial convention for the current project, not a claim about every publishing system. We also need to repair subject aliases, test reader navigation and reconcile the cover metadata. The old print page numbers cannot simply be copied into every electronic link because the reader may change font size and reflow the text.

I will apply the current convention of ignoring initial articles for sorting while preserving the full displayed title. The order key and title string are distinct fields. Alias relationships, navigation behavior and cover metadata will have separate review records so an approved sorting rule is not mistaken for a completed or correct ebook.

The print index has entries Orchard care and Fruit-tree care that refer to the same section. The editor proposes making the second a see reference to the first. Another pair, Bank as a river edge and Bank as a storage collection, refers to different sections despite identical words. We have not approved the alias table yet. Please keep the semantic reasons beside proposed merges so a global text deduplication does not collapse the two different Bank entries into one destination.

Record the proposed orchard alias and the two separate meanings of Bank independently. A matching title string does not establish identical subject matter. Ask the editor to approve relationships between identified entries, not a rule that merges every repeated word. A see reference can remove duplicate indexing while still directing the reader to an actual, uniquely identified destination.

Our first navigation mock-up uses a contents link, a section heading and a Back to index link at the end of each section. The mock-up was tested only by clicking through in a desktop preview. A volunteer using a different reader says the Back link may return to the start of the book instead of the index location. We have not reproduced that report. We need a test that records the reader, entry point and exact link, rather than saying navigation works because one editor could reach a section.

Preserve the successful desktop observation with its scope and open a separate reproduction task for the reported reader. Test the same path and record where Back lands. A reachable destination and a useful return path are different requirements. Do not replace the earlier pass with an assumed universal failure, or dismiss the report because it occurred on another reader.

The approved manuscript subtitle is A Guide to Shared Gardens. The cover artwork draft says A Guide for Shared Gardens, and an old retailer listing omits the subtitle entirely. We do not know which file the retailer preview currently uses. The designer has received the correct wording but has not produced a revised cover. Please track the manuscript, artwork and listing as separate artifacts rather than declaring every appearance corrected when one person receives the text.

The manuscript supports the subtitle wording, while the cover and listing need their own changes and checks. Keep the old artwork and listing identified as mismatches. A message carrying the correct wording is useful evidence of a request, not evidence that a rendered cover or live preview has incorporated it. First establish which actual file feeds the preview.

The editor approved the orchard alias after comparing the two section references. Fruit-tree care will point to Orchard care. She also confirmed that the two Bank meanings must remain separate, and suggested adding qualifiers in the display labels. We assigned draft identifiers ORC, BNK-R and BNK-S. These are working identifiers, not yet an approved cross-reference standard. The exported index still has the older unqualified Bank rows because no new file has been generated from the table.

The semantic relationships are approved, with identifier conventions and export implementation still distinct decisions. Preserve the separate river and storage targets even if the visible labels are similar. A later export should be checked against those approved relationships; updating the alias spreadsheet does not itself repair hyperlinks or rename rows in an existing ebook file.

We reproduced the Back-link report on the second reader. Opening a section from the index works, but Back returns to the book's front because it targets a generic start anchor. The desktop editor had used the reader's own navigation-history button during the earlier check, not the book's Back link. Both observations were real but tested different controls. We will revise the test sheet to distinguish built-in reader history from links embedded in our content.

The discrepancy is explained by the different return controls. Keep the desktop observation, but do not cite it as a pass for the embedded link. The content link needs a specific index destination, and the revised test should exercise it directly. Reader history can remain a convenience without becoming a substitute for a broken feature in the ebook.

The designer sent revised cover artwork with the manuscript's subtitle. We compared the editable text layer and found the right wording. In the small thumbnail, however, the line is clipped after Shared. The full cover looks correct at its intended dimensions. The retailer needs both files, so the designer will adjust the thumbnail crop separately. We have not approved the package or asked the retailer to refresh anything yet.

The full cover passes its wording check, while the thumbnail fails a presentation check. Keep those results separate and request a revised crop. A correctly spelled source text layer is not sufficient if a required output hides part of the title. Wait for the checked package before asking for a preview refresh that could otherwise distribute another incomplete artifact.

A volunteer used the printed handbook's page numbers to make a draft list of link destinations. On a larger font setting in the ebook, those page references no longer align with the intended section starts. The text itself is present; this is a destination-addressing problem, not missing content. The developer proposes named entry anchors that remain attached to the sections. We have not decided the naming convention or whether the same anchors can support both index and contents links.

The font-size trial shows why print page numbers are fragile electronic addresses. Named anchors are a promising alternative, but their scheme needs a uniqueness and persistence check. Preserve the old page mapping as source context while testing actual targets in a new export. A proposal to add anchors does not establish that existing links already reach them.

I found the copyeditor's ordering note for the current index. It places A Garden under Garden and The Orchard under Orchard, explaining that initial articles are omitted from the sort key while left in the displayed titles. This is the same current convention as the original project note, written with examples. The note also discusses a title beginning with Art, where those first letters form part of a word; that title is not an instruction to strip any prefix that merely looks similar to an article.

The examples and their explanation repeat the current article-ignoring sort policy. The Art example marks a boundary: a complete initial article is different from a few matching letters inside a word. Keep the rule and the examples together so a simplistic prefix operation cannot remove meaningful text or silently alter the displayed titles.

The developer implemented draft anchors for the orchard section and both Bank sections. A link test reached the intended river-bank heading, but the storage-bank anchor accidentally reused the same identifier. The exported file therefore sends both Bank rows to the river section. We marked that build unsuitable for distribution. The editor's decision to keep the meanings separate remains correct; the implementation did not preserve it. The developer has proposed a suffix correction but has not built it yet.

The repeated anchor is an implementation collision, not evidence that the two subjects should merge. Correct the storage target and verify each link independently in a fresh build. Keep the faulty export identified so it is not confused with the spreadsheet's correct relationships. The proposed suffix alone does not prove which anchor appears in the next generated file.

We changed the embedded Back link to target the index heading and generated a navigation test file. It returns correctly when the section is opened from the index on the second reader. If the same section is opened from the contents list, Back still goes to the index rather than the contents. That matches the visible label Back to index, so the editor considers it intended behavior. We should not claim it dynamically returns to whichever place a reader came from.

The observed link satisfies its named destination on the tested reader. Keep the label explicit so users do not expect browser-like history behavior. The test can cover both entry paths without treating a fixed index destination as a defect. Other reader configurations still need their own checks before we describe the link as generally reliable across the supported set.

The revised thumbnail now shows the full subtitle, but it includes a faint printer crop mark at one corner. The full cover file has no such mark. The designer offered a quick paint-over, while the production editor prefers a clean export from the artwork. We chose the clean-export approach and requested it. No replacement thumbnail has arrived. The existing full-cover wording check need not be repeated solely because the thumbnail still requires repair.

Requesting a clean export specifies a remedy without claiming completion. Keep the full cover's passed check and the thumbnail's open defect attached to their separate files. When the new thumbnail arrives, inspect both the crop mark and the subtitle visibility, since a correction to one feature could inadvertently restore the other defect.

The developer corrected the duplicate Bank anchor and supplied a new test export. The river row now reaches the river section, and the storage row reaches the collection-storage section in the desktop preview. We have not tested the corrected export on the second reader. The alias Fruit-tree care still points to a printed page number because that row was missed during conversion. Its subject relationship is approved, but its electronic destination remains wrong.

The Bank correction passes the desktop link check without establishing cross-reader behavior. Repair the missed orchard alias destination and keep its semantic approval separate from address implementation. Each identified row can have a different readiness state. A successful test of two links is not evidence that every reference in the conversion table was updated.

The clean thumbnail arrived without the crop mark and with the subtitle visible. The production editor approved the full-cover and thumbnail pair as package C2. We saved both files with their package identifier. The retailer preview is still using an older package; the account contact has not requested a refresh. Approval of C2 tells us which assets are ready to send, not what remote viewers currently see.

C2 is an approved source package, while the retailer preview is a separate downstream artifact. Prepare a request identifying both files and ask for confirmation of the received version. Keep a screenshot or other observation of the later preview when it is available, because a receipt acknowledgment does not guarantee that the intended files were rendered.

A reader using enlarged text found the contents hierarchy confusing: subsection headings looked like separate chapters because they had identical levels in the navigation tree. The manuscript marks them as subsections. We corrected the structure in the editable document and asked the developer for another export. The visible font sizes had looked different, but the semantic navigation levels were wrong. Please keep the tree-level defect distinct from visual typography and from the already tested Back link.

The manuscript supports the hierarchy change. Test the generated navigation tree after export rather than assuming visible size differences communicate structural levels to every reader. The fixed Back destination remains a different feature. A new build can preserve one improvement while introducing or retaining another defect, so the evidence should identify what was actually exercised.

The editor approved the cross-reference design: link targets must use stable entry identifiers rather than page numbers. Each identifier must name one subject destination, and renaming a displayed label should not create a different target. The approved scheme keeps river bank and storage bank distinct. This is a design decision; the unfinished orchard alias and enlarged-text hierarchy still need implementation checks. We have not approved the current export for release.

The accepted design uses stable identifiers for cross-references. Preserve those bindings when titles or pagination change, and test actual exported anchors against the approved table. The design resolves how destinations should be addressed, not whether every row already complies. Existing conversion defects remain open until their specific outputs have been checked.

The orchard alias now points to its stable entry identifier in a new export. A desktop check follows Fruit-tree care to Orchard care correctly. We then changed the displayed heading to Caring for an Orchard in a test branch without changing the identifier, and the link still worked. That experiment supports the intended independence from heading wording. It is not an approved change to the book's displayed heading; the release branch keeps the editor's existing wording.

The test demonstrates the stable-target behavior while preserving the distinction between a test-branch rename and an editorial decision. Keep the release text unchanged unless the editor approves a rename. The successful desktop result should be recorded with the test build, and the release export still needs comparison to ensure it carries the accepted identifier without the temporary heading.

The retailer contact submitted C2 and received an automated upload acknowledgment. The account page says processing. No refreshed preview is visible yet. The contact wondered whether the acknowledgment proves the old subtitle has disappeared; it does not show a rendered result. We will check the actual preview when processing finishes. The upload request was authorized, but no one should announce a corrected retailer listing on the basis of the acknowledgment alone.

The package handoff has an observed upload acknowledgment, with rendering pending. Keep the source assets and receipt identifier together so a later mismatch can be investigated. Inspect the actual preview for subtitle wording and thumbnail crop after it appears. An accepted upload and a correct public display are separate stages in this workflow.

The enlarged-text export now nests the subsections under their chapters in the navigation tree. The reader confirmed the hierarchy but found that one subsection's return link is missing because its source paragraph was accidentally deleted during restructuring. Other sections still have their tested links. We restored the missing paragraph in the editable document. A new export has not been generated. The hierarchy pass remains valid for the tested build, while the missing return needs a separate repair check.

Record the hierarchy improvement and the missing-link defect without collapsing them into a single pass or fail label for every feature. After export, test the restored subsection link and verify that the intended nesting persists. A source restoration is a proposed output correction until the resulting ebook is inspected. Do not assume that unrelated links were removed merely because one paragraph was lost.

The editor reviewed the qualified Bank labels and preferred Bank—river edge and Bank—stored collection over the abbreviated draft labels. She approved those visible labels without changing the destination identifiers. The alias table was updated, but a screenshot in the review guide still shows the old abbreviated names. That screenshot is teaching documentation rather than an actual hyperlink table. We need to replace it so reviewers know which labels to look for in the next export.

The label wording decision leaves the two subject identities intact. Update the guide screenshot from an observed build rather than editing text over an old image and implying it was captured from the current file. The stale screenshot could mislead a reviewer, but it does not itself change the live anchors or prove that a link is wrong.

The new export contains the restored subsection return link. On the second reader, that link reaches the index heading, and the revised navigation hierarchy is still present. We also checked that the temporary Caring for an Orchard heading from the test branch is absent from the release file. The release heading uses the editor's approved wording. We have not yet tested the two qualified Bank rows on this reader, so their desktop passes should remain scoped to the earlier checks.

The restored link, hierarchy and release-heading selection have documented results for this export. Leave the Bank cross-reader tests open rather than assuming shared infrastructure guarantees identical behavior. Keep the exact file identifier in the review record so the next person does not accidentally test an older collision build or the branch containing the temporary heading.

The retailer preview finished processing. Its full cover now shows the correct subtitle, but the thumbnail still uses the old cropped version. The contact checked the C2 upload record and found both correct source files attached, so the discrepancy appears in the downstream preview. We have asked the retailer contact to request a thumbnail refresh, with the observed mismatch attached. The book has not been launched. The full-cover improvement remains real even though the thumbnail needs another action.

Preserve the separate full-cover and thumbnail observations. The correct uploaded pair does not prove the rendered thumbnail is current. Request a targeted refresh using the existing approved asset rather than revising an already correct source file without reason. Do not describe the entire preview as corrected or the launch as completed while the displayed mismatch remains.

A contributor found that the phrase river bank appears in a chapter discussing picnic seating as well as in the technical river-edge section. She suggested making both occurrences index targets under the same qualified entry. The editor wants to review whether the picnic passage adds useful subject coverage or merely repeats a word. No new target has been approved. The existing river-edge destination remains unchanged while this proposed expansion is considered.

Keep the proposed coverage expansion separate from repairing a broken link. The editor may choose an additional relevant reference, but word occurrence alone does not establish that it should become a subject destination. Until that decision, preserve the current approved target and do not label the index incomplete merely because every repeated phrase is not separately linked.

We captured a fresh guide screenshot from the release export showing the qualified Bank labels. The image itself is accurate, but the guide caption still names the old test build. We corrected the editable caption and have not regenerated the guide PDF. The reviewer training session is only proposed. Please do not treat an accurate screenshot as a fully corrected guide if the surrounding text points people toward the wrong file.

The current screenshot can be retained while the caption and PDF export are corrected. Verify that the resulting guide identifies the actual reviewed build. This is a documentation consistency check, distinct from the ebook's own link tests. A proposed training session should use the corrected guide when it exists, not create an assumption that the session has already occurred.

The editor rejected adding the picnic-seating passage as another river-bank target because it does not discuss the indexed subject. She accepted a short explanatory note in the editorial log so the suggestion is not reopened solely from a keyword search. No content was removed from the chapter. The two qualified Bank entries remain distinct and their destination identifiers unchanged. This decision concerns index coverage, not a different sorting convention or a new name for either subject.

The reviewed coverage decision preserves the existing target without deleting the underlying passage. Keep the rejection reason with the proposal. A future substantive change could justify another review, but repeated word matching alone is not new evidence. The subject distinction and stable identifiers remain the operative design for the unresolved cross-reader checks.

The second-reader test of the river-bank row passed. The storage-bank row failed because the reader used an older cached navigation file despite showing the new visible label. Clearing that reader's cache and reopening the same export made the storage link reach the correct section. We recorded both observations. The developer asks for a cold-open test on a different device before closing the issue, because the cache remedy should not be mistaken for proof that every user will receive the new navigation data.

The evidence distinguishes a stale cached navigation path from the current file's successful reopened path. Keep the requested cold-open test pending. Do not rewrite the old failure as if it never happened, but also do not conclude that the approved identifier table is wrong solely from the stale state. The next test should specify installation and cache conditions.

The retailer contact acknowledged the thumbnail refresh request but has not supplied a new preview. We saved the request and the observed old thumbnail. A marketing volunteer proposed distributing a direct image of the correct C2 cover in the meantime; that would be a different asset placement, not correction of the retailer thumbnail. The editor has not approved the temporary marketing workaround. The launch date remains unset.

Track the refresh acknowledgment separately from an observed new thumbnail. The workaround proposal may be considered on its own terms, without claiming it repairs the retailer's cached image. Continue using the checked source package for any authorized preparation, and leave launch or distribution decisions to their actual approvals rather than deriving them from a support reply.

The guide PDF was regenerated with the corrected build caption, and a colleague compared that caption with the screenshot's source record. The guide is ready for internal reviewer training. The coordinator scheduled an internal session for a later date but has not held it. During preparation, she noticed the test checklist lacks a box for noting whether a device was opened cold or restored from a previous session. We can amend that checklist before training without changing the ebook itself.

The guide caption check is complete, while the training and checklist addition are future work. Add the cold-open condition to the checklist so the pending storage-link test is reproducible. The new checklist field is prompted by an observed cache issue; it should not be treated as an unrelated demand to repeat every verified link under arbitrary conditions.

The reviewer borrowed a different reader for the cold-open storage-bank test, but its battery failed during setup before the ebook was opened. The test has no navigation result. We returned the device for charging and kept the requested observation open. The failed setup does not invalidate the successful cache-cleared test or prove a link defect. Please propose the next concrete arrangement for the cold-open test, naming which export and which entry need observation rather than merely saying test everything again.

Arrange a usable device and open the identified release export without a restored session, then exercise the storage-bank link and record its destination. Treat the battery interruption as a setup event with no link verdict. The river-bank result and the earlier reopened storage result can remain in the evidence table with their original conditions.

The retailer contact sent a preview-package link claiming the thumbnail was refreshed. We have not opened that package in the review environment yet, so we do not know whether its files differ from the last observed preview. The source package C2 remains approved. The production editor wants a comparison of the actual cover and thumbnail rather than relying on the email subject line. No launch authorization was attached to the message.

Inspect the received preview package and compare its rendered subtitle and thumbnail with the approved assets. A message saying refreshed is evidence of a claim, not a visual verification result. Keep launch authority separate. If the files still differ, report the actual discrepancy and identifiers instead of silently accepting the claim or inventing a new source revision.

The training coordinator added a cold-open checkbox to the test sheet, but the wording says fresh file rather than fresh reader session. Those are not the same condition: our cache issue occurred with the same ebook export. We changed the editable wording to opened without restoring a prior reader session. The printed training sheets still have the ambiguous phrase, and the internal training has been postponed until corrected sheets are available. It has not taken place.

Print and inspect the clarified checklist before rescheduling the internal training. Preserve the ebook export identifier separately from the reader-session condition. The distinction lets a later tester reproduce the intended cold-open observation without incorrectly assuming a different file must be generated. A postponed training session is not a completed calibration exercise.

A helper offered to combine the alias decisions, sorting note and navigation log into one abbreviated handoff. We asked for a draft first rather than declaring every sentence dependent on every source it could see. The handoff should keep test-branch experiments, approved labels, observed link results and pending preview checks distinct. It should identify historical examples as such and avoid turning a source filename or a reviewer promise into a present implementation result.

When the draft exists, check its actual claims and evidence links. A note about the current index policy may depend on the ordering record, while a preview-inspection task can depend only on the cover correspondence. Shared access during drafting is not enough to establish semantic dependence. Keep the useful task boundaries and assess any copied policy or historical example according to its actual content.
