The attendance sheet supports a teaching-role attribution to Elin Mora, subject to the document's own scope. It does not by itself establish who created any named transition. Preserve that distinction in the handoff: a person can teach a sequence without being its creator. The missing connection between the attendance sheet and a notation version is a separate provenance question, not a reason to erase its labeled role.

The notation editor approved a new rule: facing direction and travel direction must use separate symbols. In legend N2, a short pointer shows facing and a path arrow shows travel. She approved that distinction but asked us to test the sequence in context. We have not yet received a reader's reconstruction using N2, so approval of the rule is narrower than approval of the whole score.

N2 establishes a clear distinction for the handoff while leaving full-sequence reconstruction open. Keep the editor's approval attached to the legend version, and do not transfer it to an old sheet with one unlabelled arrow. The next useful evidence would be a reader's interpretation linked to N2, ideally describing both where the dancer faces and where the movement takes the dancer.

I asked reader Tomas to reconstruct the transition from N2 without watching F1. He confirmed receipt and asked whether the page is drawn from the audience or dancer perspective. I realized that the new legend still does not state the viewing perspective. I have asked the editor which convention she intended; Tomas has paused the exercise rather than submitting a failed reconstruction.

Tomas has identified an unresolved coordinate convention before completing the task. That pause is not evidence that the separate symbols failed. Clarify the viewing perspective with the editor and issue an identifiable revision before asking him to continue. Keep his receipt separate from an actual reconstruction, and do not fill in his intended movements from the editor's probable preference.

I contacted the archive desk asking for a creation-credit record associated with the transition. The desk acknowledged the request and gave it ticket K14. The reply says their catalog search has not started yet. I did not attach the attendance sheet as proof of creation; I only mentioned it as a possible route to identifying the relevant rehearsal folder.

Ticket K14 demonstrates receipt of a search request, not a completed search or a verified credit. The attendance sheet may help locate material, but its teaching-role label remains unchanged. Keep a future catalog result distinct from the existing working attribution note. If no creation record is found, that absence alone would not establish a different author either.

The media volunteer found a file called side-angle-preview. It opens as a low-resolution contact sheet with still frames, not a playable side-camera clip. One frame appears to show the rear dancer's shoes, but its timestamp is cropped out. I have asked for the underlying video file. At present we have only a still-image lead, not a replacement reference segment.

The contact sheet suggests that another view may exist, while leaving its timing and continuous movement unavailable. Record it as a lead and retain the exact filename so a later file can be linked to the request. A visible shoe in a still frame cannot establish the sequence of steps. The underlying video request remains open, and F1's obstruction has not been resolved.

The editor clarified that the chart should use the dancer's perspective. She revised the heading to say this explicitly in N3 and retained the separate facing and travel symbols. Tomas has N3 now. He says the heading is clear, but he has not sent his reconstruction because his practice session is scheduled for later. I am keeping that future appointment separate from completed review evidence.

N3 resolves the declared viewing convention, and Tomas's response supports readability of its heading. His movement reconstruction is still pending. Preserve the version link between his future notes and N3; a statement that the heading is clear does not demonstrate that every directional mark is correct. The editor's clarification also does not turn the old front-camera video into a mirrored view of the chart.

The media volunteer sent a playable side-camera clip S1. The file begins before the rehearsal count-in and continues through the transition. I can see the rear dancer's feet, but the sound starts late. I cannot use the first audible count as time zero without comparing it to the visible count-in. I have not made that comparison yet.

S1 addresses the visual obstruction, but the sound offset creates a new alignment question. Work from identifiable visual actions or a documented offset rather than assuming the audio begins with the movement. The file's arrival is not a completed alignment. A careful handoff can say that an unobstructed side view is available while identifying which synchronization check is still needed.

The archive desk says K14 has reached the catalog team. They have found a folder title matching our rehearsal location, but not yet a document containing the transition name. I have sent the alternate spelling used in the old folder index. Their message neither confirms the working creation credit nor says that the attendance sheet was wrong.

That update is progress in locating a possible folder, not a decision about authorship. Keep the alternate spelling in the search correspondence as a search key, rather than treating it as a second independently verified work. The teaching-role entry remains a separate document claim. A successful folder-name match does not automatically establish that every item inside belongs to the same notation version.

For the exercise's provisional catalog line, I shortened the working note to Pivot Bridge — E. Mora, creation credit unverified. The abbreviation expands to Elin Mora in the folder's local name key. The name key also includes other people who attended the rehearsal. I have not replaced the unverified label with confirmed merely because the abbreviated line looks more formal.

That catalog line credits Pivot Bridge to E. Mora, still marked as an unverified creation credit. Its abbreviated name can be expanded through the local key, so it is not independent evidence. Keep the qualification visible. An attendance list containing a person's name, without the creation-credit relation, would not have the same meaning as this line linking the named transition to that person.

Tomas submitted an N3 reconstruction. He kept his facing pointer consistent, but he moved left when the travel path on row C requires right in dancer perspective. He explained that he read the chart while looking into a wall mirror. The editor wants to add a short no-mirror reading instruction before testing again. We have not yet received a second reconstruction.

The first reconstruction reveals an interaction between the declared perspective and the mirror used during reading. Preserve Tomas's explanation and the row-C observation without treating it as a failure of every symbol. A no-mirror instruction is a proposed correction to the exercise conditions. It should be issued with a version identifier and tested before reporting that the directional confusion is resolved.

I compared S1's visible count-in with the first audible count. The soundtrack begins two beats after the visible start gesture. I wrote that observation in an alignment note, with frame stills for the start and the first audible count. I have not shifted the actual video or asked anyone to accept an edited track as an original archive recording.

The note supplies an observed alignment offset for this clip, not a new original media file. It can guide review of the movement without rewriting the archive recording. Preserve the stills and distinguish a proposed synchronized viewing copy from the unchanged source clip. The two-beat finding does not by itself validate the old misplaced time link in the working document.

The archive desk sent a scan of the attendance sheet we already have. The scan is sharper, but its heading is still rehearsal teacher. There is no creation-credit field in the margin or on the reverse side. I asked the desk to keep K14 open for the actual request rather than closing it as fulfilled by a cleaner copy of a different kind of document.

A sharper copy improves legibility of the teaching record without changing its evidential scope. It should not be counted as a second independent source for a creation credit. Keeping K14 open is consistent with the unanswered request. The handoff can retain the documented teaching role and still state that the separate creation-credit inquiry has not been answered by the returned scan.

I drafted an internal reviewer checklist: confirm N3's intended perspective, inspect the rear dancer's footwork in S1, and verify where the old time link lands. Those are checks, not completed outcomes. The checklist has a box for each item, but I left them blank because the people named as reviewers have not returned results. The existence of three boxes does not mean three tests passed.

The checklist organizes work already motivated by the source defects. Keep its boxes tied to actual returned evidence when reviews occur, rather than treating the list itself as a summary of success. The alignment observation can inform the footwork review, while the notation perspective and the document link each need their own verification. A proposed assignment does not prove that a reviewer has accepted or performed it.

The editor issued N4 with a no-mirror instruction above the dancer-perspective heading. Tomas received it and completed another reconstruction. His travel and facing descriptions now match rows A through C, but row D is not in his response because the printout stopped at the page break. This is a partial success, not a full reconstruction of the transition.

The returned N4 exercise supports the first three rows under the revised reading instruction. The missing row D is a material-availability gap, not an observed directional error. Ask for the complete page or a joined view and have Tomas finish the remaining row. Do not discard the supported earlier rows, and do not claim the entire sequence passed because the returned portion matched.

The media reviewer checked the unobstructed footwork in S1 against the row-C travel description. She confirms the visible movement supports that row. She did not assess row D because her review brief only named row C. I saved her exact scope note. I also asked the document editor to repair the old link, but she has not sent a revised document.

The media result closes the specified row-C check and should not be expanded to unreviewed rows. The link repair remains requested, while the source video and alignment note remain available. The next work can target missing row-D evidence or the actual navigation link, rather than reassigning the already completed row-C review as though no response had been received.

The archive desk says the relevant folder has not yielded a creation-credit document. They emphasize that the search is incomplete because one box is not yet available. The local teaching record is legible, but its content has not changed. I do not want the handoff to interpret an incomplete search as proof that a credited person did not create the work.

Keep the negative search result bounded by the unavailable box and the incomplete process. It does not confirm the working attribution, disprove it, or supply a replacement creator. The documented teaching role can still be reported for its own purpose. An accurate handoff can identify what remains to be searched without inventing a conclusive attribution from a lack of results so far.

A rehearsal handout separately introduces Elin Mora as the teacher who demonstrated the warm-up exercise. It does not name Pivot Bridge and does not describe the warm-up as her creation. This is useful for a teaching-history sidebar, but I want it kept out of the creation-evidence column. The document editor says that separating those columns makes the record easier to understand.

The handout provides evidence about a teaching role rather than a creation credit. Reusing the person's name in that independent role need not assert authorship. Preserve the document's actual wording and subject, especially because it names a warm-up rather than the transition under review. A clear column distinction helps prevent an identity match from being treated as evidence that two different predicates are equivalent.

Tomas received a joined-page N4 view and supplied the missing row D. His description matches the editor's intended facing and travel directions. The editor has accepted the completed reconstruction as a single-reader check. It does not establish historical authorship or prove that every future reader will perform the score correctly, but the requested N4 exercise is now complete.

That closes the specific missing-row task while preserving its limited scope. The N4 reconstruction can be cited as a completed readability check for this reader and version. There is no need to keep requesting his absent row D after it has arrived. Separate that result from historical provenance, other readers' usability, and any remaining issue with how the video is linked in the handoff document.

The document editor sent handoff H2 with a new time link. It now opens S1 rather than F1, but the browser player drops the fragment when the link is copied into the exported PDF. Clicking in her editable document works; clicking in my PDF opens S1 at its beginning. I have not accepted the PDF export as navigation-ready.

This narrows the link problem to the export route rather than the underlying clip selection. Keep both observed behaviors: the editable document seeks correctly, while the exported PDF does not. A repair should be verified in the delivery format recipients will actually use. Do not call the link fixed solely on the editor's successful test in a different document format.

The archive desk has scheduled access to the remaining box for a future reading-room appointment. No inspection has happened yet, and the appointment is not a guarantee that a creation-credit record exists. I asked for the box reference and appointment details to be attached to K14 so the next archivist can continue the request without guessing what was promised.

The appointment is a concrete next step in an unfinished search. Retain its scope without converting it into a positive finding. The handoff can ask the next archivist to record what is actually inspected when access occurs. Until then, neither the working attribution nor the separate teaching-role documents have acquired additional authorship evidence merely because access has been scheduled.

The access copy of S1 is silent when opened on the archive kiosk because that station has muted playback. The visible count-in and footwork remain viewable. A volunteer assumed the audio track was missing from the file, but I checked the same file on another station and heard it. I want this recorded as a playback-setting observation, not a new damaged-source allegation.

The cross-station check distinguishes a local playback condition from absence of an audio track. Keep the original source file unchanged and avoid replacing it on that assumption. The known sound offset still exists where audio is audible, while the kiosk's mute setting is a separate interface issue. A viewing instruction can mention the station behavior without claiming that the recorded rehearsal had no sound.

The document editor produced PDF H3 with a plain video URL plus written seek instructions instead of relying only on the dropped fragment. I tested it on the archive kiosk: the clip opens, and following the written position reaches the intended transition. I sent the result back. That navigation test is complete for the kiosk; we have not tested the external reviewer's device.

H3 now has an observed working navigation route on the archive kiosk. The written seek instruction is a documented workaround, not proof that every PDF viewer preserves fragments. Keep the successful test and its platform scope. A further device check can be proposed if needed, but the handoff should not describe the kiosk route as still broken after your actual test succeeded.

The archive manager asks whether the working note, attendance scan, and rehearsal handout can be flattened into one short credit line. I declined for now because they make different kinds of claims. I suggested separate columns for working creation attribution, documented teaching roles, and search status. We have not received a new creation record from the reading-room visit, which is still ahead.

Separate columns preserve the distinction among an unverified credit, an explicitly labeled teaching role, and an unfinished search. Flattening them would erase uncertainty and predicate differences. The handoff can carry those categories without assuming that one document corroborates another merely because the same person's name appears. The planned reading-room visit remains a future evidence-gathering step rather than a completed provenance check.

We found a duplicate H3 attachment in a volunteer's mailbox named H3-approved. The volunteer explains that approved was her personal reminder that the kiosk link worked. The archive manager has not signed off the final handoff package. I asked the volunteer to use the actual test note instead of adding global approval language to the filename.

A local filename should not be treated as a manager's package approval. Preserve the valid kiosk result while correcting the scope implied by the name. The requested renaming is not yet confirmed, and the manager's final review is still absent. It would be unfair to discard a real navigation test simply because someone overstated it, but equally inaccurate to promote that test to full release authorization.

The proposed release package includes the N4 notation, H3 handoff PDF, and an access copy of S1. The archive manager wants a checksum list before review. I have generated hashes for N4 and H3, but the media volunteer is still copying S1 to the release folder. I have not hashed the destination file because it is not there yet.

The package-integrity step is partially complete. Keep the two existing hashes tied to the exact files they describe, and wait for the destination media file before generating its hash. A hash of another copy would not by itself demonstrate successful transfer to the release folder. The manager's requested review cannot be treated as completed merely because the package contents have been listed.

The S1 transfer finished, and I generated a checksum for the destination file. It matches the source-copy checksum supplied by the media volunteer. That verifies the copied bytes under this comparison; it is not a fresh performance or authorship review. I assembled the three-file checksum list and sent it to the archive manager. No package approval has arrived yet.

The destination transfer check and the complete checksum list are now supported. Do not keep the media copy listed as missing. The open release dependency is the archive manager's response to the assembled package, distinct from the completed technical checks. A next action can request that decision or clarify its scope without inventing approval from the successful byte comparison.

The external reviewer tried H3 on a phone and says the written seek position is readable, but the tiny row labels in N4 become blurred when zoomed. She has not attempted a reconstruction from that display. I asked the editor for a high-resolution notation page or a text alternative. The new accessibility request does not undo Tomas's completed paper-based exercise.

This introduces a display-accessibility issue on a different device, with a clear distinction from earlier readability evidence. The reviewer has not supplied a failed movement reconstruction; she could not read the row labels well enough to begin. A higher-resolution page or text alternative could address that barrier, but neither has been delivered. Keep the known successful paper exercise and the unresolved phone-display issue side by side.

The archive desk confirms that the remaining box is reserved for the planned appointment, but the archivist has not visited yet. The manager asked whether our release decision must wait for that search. I sent back a request for her explicit choice about publishing an exercise package with provenance qualifications. I have not made that choice on her behalf.

The box reservation is not an inspected record, and the manager's question is not a release decision. The handoff can identify the pending policy choice while keeping the factual state of the search unchanged. An authorized decision to release a qualified exercise package, if later made, would still not verify a creation credit. At present both the response and the inspection remain absent.

The media volunteer asked whether to repair the original S1 soundtrack offset before archiving it. I asked him to preserve the original and, if a synchronized viewing copy is needed, make a separately labeled derivative with the offset documented. He has not created that derivative. The current package still contains the previously checked access copy, not a silently retimed original.

That instruction preserves the distinction between the recorded source and a possible convenience derivative. It creates a proposed media task, not a new synchronized file. The existing alignment note and the verified navigation route remain usable for review. Any later derivative should carry its own version and relationship to S1; its creation would not change the observation that the original soundtrack begins later than the visible start gesture.

creation_note: Original fictional evaluation script; all people, institutions, dates and dialogue are authored. No real participant log or public provenance is claimed.

haystack_sessions.content: For our fictional Harbour Puzzle Hunt, the current scoring policy subtracts one point per requested hint. This is the rule entered in the administration workbook, not a report of anyone winning. I want a handoff that follows evidence through revisions. We have three separate jobs: reconcile outage receipts, check the scoring calculator, and prevent public aliases from colliding on the display.

I would start the policy note from full score and remove a point for each hint requested. That sentence is a paraphrase of the rule you supplied. The receipt ledger should be a separate table, so a witness correction does not silently edit a score formula. A display alias should point to a stable team identifier, rather than serve as that identifier.

The first paper packet has receipts E11 through E16. E13 appears twice: one blue carbon copy says station East and a white original says station West. Both sheets bear initials, but the packet does not contain a witness roster. Do not guess that the second sheet is fraudulent. I put the two copies in separate sleeves and recorded their physical positions in the packet.

We can mark the two E13 sheets as an unresolved sequence collision. My proposed worksheet would have columns for physical sheet, station, signer, visible time and later interpretation. Keeping observation apart from interpretation lets a witness explain duplicate numbering without our overwriting either sheet. I have not inspected an original signature or contacted a station volunteer; these are suggested follow-up steps only.

Calculator file calc-a reads the Hints column when it displays the Solves total. I found this by typing a dummy row with four solved puzzles and no hint requests: its displayed solves became zero. That is a reproduction of a column-reference defect, not a result from the hunt. I saved the row under fixtures, away from participant submissions, and left the broken workbook unchanged.

That dummy row is useful because it separates two input dimensions. Before editing a formula, duplicate the workbook and note exactly which cell reference changes. A score output alone would not tell us whether the wrong source column or the deduction expression caused the problem. The original fixture should remain available to demonstrate the earlier defect when a reviewer checks the repair.

The public mock-up also contains two teams called Lantern. Their stable identifiers are T-amber and T-copper; the registration sheets show different captains. I have not chosen replacement display names. The archived mock-up screenshot therefore remains ambiguous if read without those identifiers. Its file name includes practice, but the page title inside the image just says standings, which could mislead a reader.

Keep both actual team records and flag the display collision. A temporary table can use stable identifiers in a separate column while the captains choose aliases. For the screenshot, an archive caption can identify it as an unresolved practice mock-up without altering the image. That would preserve evidence of the display defect and avoid presenting its ambiguous rows as a final public result.

We have now approved this tie-handling requirement: answers submitted during a server outage must use the signed offline receipt order. The rule concerns outage answers, not ordinary online arrivals. The witness roster has arrived and shows that East and West used independent stationery pads. It does not resolve which E13 sheet belongs earlier in the combined sequence; their pad numbers are local counters, not a global clock.

The separate pad explanation makes accidental numbering overlap plausible, but does not establish combined arrival order. I suggest linking each sheet to its named witness and using the signed order evidence rather than sorting raw pad numbers. If a combined order is absent, the handoff should retain an unresolved position instead of turning a station-specific counter into an unsupported tie decision.

The coordinator has written a combined order sheet for E11, East E13, E12 and West E13. Only the coordinator has signed it. One East volunteer annotated that E12 came before East E13, with an arrow but no date. I scanned both pages together so the annotation stays associated with its parent sheet. Neither station volunteer has counter-signed the coordinator's proposed combined order.

This is a proposed reconciliation, not yet the required signed agreement. The arrow should be transcribed as an annotation by the East volunteer, not as our independent observation of arrival. It would help to ask that volunteer to explain the arrow and then have the relevant witnesses review the combined sequence. Until then, the ledger can store the proposal alongside the untouched sheets.

In calc-b I changed the Solves display reference to the Solves column. The dummy row now displays four solves, and a second row with no solves but several requests no longer masquerades as solved work. I have not checked the final score cells. The revision log says display-reference repair only. Please do not convert that limited check into a statement that the complete calculator is certified.

The repaired display has two observed fixture outcomes, while scoring arithmetic remains open. A separate test tab can record expected outputs before recalculation, then compare actual cells after the workbook opens. The distinction matters because correcting a visible total can leave a hidden score expression pointing at the old column. We should preserve the limited scope in the workbook's approval field.

The two Lantern captains answered our alias request. T-amber accepts Lantern East; T-copper prefers Copper Kite. Their replies approve only their own display names, not publication of full registration sheets. I entered the names into a draft map but have not rebuilt the scoreboard. The archive screenshot stays in its original folder with the new explanatory caption in a separate text file.

The reply permissions support the display-name map and do not justify exposing registration details. A rebuild should take identifiers as its join keys and names as presentation fields. When checking the result, look for both distinct rows and correct score association. A cosmetic rename can appear successful while joining an old score to the wrong newly named team.

Both station witnesses met and counter-signed a revised order sheet for the four disputed early sheets. The correction places E12 ahead of East E13. I have attached the dated witness page and marked the coordinator-only proposal superseded. This resolves that specific collision. A different receipt, E14, has a printed time on the original that differs from the handwritten carbon-copy time, and neither witness addressed E14 during the meeting.

We can close the early-sheet ordering issue with the counter-signed page as evidence. E14 needs its own open item because the meeting's signature scope names only the four listed sheets. I would not infer approval of every receipt in the packet. The original and carbon-copy times should both remain visible in an evidence table until a witness explains their different origins.

For the next calculator test I supplied a row with five solved puzzles and three hint requests. The score sheet behaved like it had counted the hint requests as solved puzzles before applying its deduction. I traced that error to a second stale reference in the ScoreBase cell, distinct from the display cell repaired last week. The workbook now has two tracked defects, not a regression of the same edited cell.

That distinction should appear in the revision log. One repair changed what the operator saw; the other must change the basis used by the score expression. I suggest a fixture matrix where solve count and request count vary independently, including empty fields. Do not use a real team's archived score as the sole expected result, because its underlying inputs might themselves be disputed.

I have copied calc-b to calc-c and repaired ScoreBase to read completed solves. The five-solve fixture now reaches the intended base calculation before deduction. I saved the displayed intermediate cells so another reviewer can reproduce it. I have not tested an empty request field or a text value in that column. The operator sheet still allows either, so the boundary behavior is important.

The handoff can list the intermediate-cell observation as a completed repair check and list blank or text requests as pending checks. If an empty value is meant to mean unknown, treating it as zero would be a policy decision rather than merely a calculation convenience. We should obtain an explicit input convention before choosing a test expectation for blanks.

The scoreboard rebuild shows Lantern East and Copper Kite as separate rows, but its footer still links to the old archive image without the companion caption. I clicked the footer from the draft page and found the ambiguous screenshot alone. The main rows were joined by stable identifiers. I therefore accepted the row mapping test but rejected the archive link presentation for public release.

A focused fix would route the footer to an archive landing page containing the original image and its practice-context caption. That retains the historical screenshot while putting its limitations in the same viewing path. We can test the landing page separately from the scoreboard join. Neither finding says anything about final standings; the current pages are administrative rehearsal artifacts.

The input convention is now written in the calculator specification: an empty request field means unknown and must display pending, while an explicit zero means no requests. The coordinator approved that convention in the document margin. It does not change the scoring policy itself. I attached the approval to calc-c's test plan and asked the operator to stop filling blank cells automatically during import.

That gives the boundary tests a defined expected distinction. We should include one genuinely blank cell and one numeric zero, not a formula that merely looks blank. A spreadsheet can coerce both to the same numeric value if the import or formula is careless. The test record needs to state the cell type as well as the visible display and expected status.

E14's carbon copy was found tucked behind E15, not in the sleeve labeled E14. The finder recorded the shelf and envelope, so we know where it was retrieved. That retrieval fact does not prove the times on either sheet. One witness thinks the handwritten time records delivery to the desk, whereas the printed time might record later data entry. We still have no counter-signed explanation.

The proposed explanation is plausible but remains a witness hypothesis. Add separate columns for claimed event type and source of that claim. If a time refers to desk delivery and another to later entry, comparing them as identical events would create a false discrepancy. The next review should ask what each clock marks, then reconcile the receipt position using the applicable signed ordering evidence.

Our coordinator's short operator draft says to begin at the full score and take away a point every time a team requests a hint. It has the same policy meaning as the administration workbook, but the draft also says blank means no requests. I marked that latter sentence for correction because it conflicts with today's approved input convention. The draft has not been distributed to operators.

I would keep the policy paraphrase and correct the separate blank-input instruction. The fact that one sentence is wrong does not make every field in the operator draft unsupported. A revision record should identify the exact input-status sentence being repaired, retain its previous version, and show which approval authorizes the correction. No operator should receive the draft while that conflicting sentence remains.

The archive landing page is built and includes the untouched screenshot, the practice caption, and a link to the current draft display. I tested it on a desktop browser and the caption was visible. The narrow-screen version hides the caption behind a collapsed panel. We have not decided whether a collapsed contextual warning is adequate for this archive; publication remains on hold.

This is an accessibility and context-presentation question, separate from data joining. A useful next test would open the archive at the smallest supported viewport without interacting first and record whether practice status is immediately perceivable. The screenshot's historical integrity need not be sacrificed to make its context accessible. We can alter the surrounding page rather than painting a correction onto the original image.

I revised the operator draft so a blank request entry yields pending review. Its hint-policy sentence remains unchanged. The draft now carries version D and the coordinator approved the input-status correction, but we have not logged delivery to operators. Please distinguish document approval from training completion; the scheduling sheet still has no named training session or attendance evidence.

The handoff can identify D as the approved document and operator training as an unscheduled next activity. If a later operator follows the retired blank rule, we will need to inspect which version reached that person, rather than assuming approval automatically changed behavior. Version availability, delivery acknowledgment and successful practice are three different observations in this workflow.

A volunteer ran the blank-cell fixture on calc-c and got the pending label. They also tried a cell containing the word none, which produced an error rather than a score. They did not run the numeric-zero fixture, explaining that it looked equivalent to blank. I added their report to the test sheet without checking the zero row myself. That remaining row is deliberately still open.

The blank result supports the unknown-input convention for that fixture only. The untested numeric zero has a different expected status, so resemblance in the interface is not enough to close it. The text error also needs a documented operator response; it might be acceptable validation or an unhelpful crash. We can record the exact message before deciding whether its behavior meets the input specification.

The E14 witness request now includes scans of both faces of both sheets. The original has a faint initials box that our first scan clipped out. A volunteer recognizes the initials but has not confirmed whether they wrote them. I have asked for a comparison against the roster signature sample. No one has changed E14's ledger position while that attribution remains unresolved.

It would be premature to label the initials an authentication. Recognition is a lead for the comparison, not a substitute for it. Keep the first clipped scan as evidence of why the question arose, but use the fuller scan for review. The ledger can link both versions and explain the clipping correction without asserting that the new image resolves the underlying event time.

The narrow-screen archive page now places practice status above the image. Two volunteers tested that at the agreed viewport and both saw the caption before opening any controls. They did not inspect every link. I accepted the caption-visibility defect as repaired, while the current-display link remains awaiting a route check after deployment to the staging host.

Those outcomes can be tracked as separate release checks. Moving the caption and seeing it at the target viewport closes that presentation issue; a link that worked locally may still resolve differently on staging. I suggest recording the staging URL, expected destination and observed page title for the remaining route check. That avoids a broad all-links-good claim based on a visual screenshot.

The staging route check failed: the archive page's current-display link pointed to a temporary file that was removed during deployment. The developer changed it to the stable scoreboard route and sent a patch. We have the patch diff but no subsequent click-through report. The main scoreboard remains visibly a rehearsal page, and its two renamed rows still map to the intended identifiers in the stored build artifact.

We should mark the route as patched but unverified. A diff establishes an intended address change, not that the deployed route resolves or serves the right page. The next tester can use the archive page as the starting point, follow the link, and compare the destination heading and team identifiers. A direct visit to the destination alone would miss an incorrect link in the archive page.

The witness who recognized E14's initials has replied that they signed the carbon copy after collecting the desk bundle. They cannot recall the exact collection time. The other witness has not replied. This gives us a claimed meaning for one signature, but not the combined signed ordering resolution we need. I am keeping E14 between two provisional rows in the internal worksheet without publishing its rank.

The reply narrows the question, but its uncertainty should remain attached. A signature after bundle collection is not necessarily an acknowledgment of every printed arrival time. Ask the second witness to compare the original scan and carbon-copy chronology rather than merely endorse a prefilled order. The provisional worksheet positions should be labeled working hypotheses so downstream staff do not mistake row order for an approved decision.

We held a document-reading session with one operator using draft D. They correctly explained that a blank input is pending and a numeric zero is different. They did not operate calc-c during the session. I have an attendance note and their written explanation, not a calculator test result. The administrator had proposed running fixtures afterward, but time ran out and nobody recorded those runs.

That is evidence of one operator's understanding of the input convention. It does not complete the zero fixture, certify all operators, or demonstrate the workbook implements the explanation. Preserve the proposed fixture session as a separate pending task. The distinction will matter if a later handoff says training was done; we can identify precisely which kind of training and what was observed.

I found a printed practice standings sheet inside the calculator folder. It predates calc-c and has handwriting on two rows, without a revision key. I moved it into the archive evidence section and recorded its original location. It should not be used as an expected-output table for the pending fixture. We have no source record explaining whether its handwritten figures were input corrections or arithmetic corrections.

The sheet can remain useful historical evidence while being unsuitable as a calculation oracle. Its unknown annotation meaning should prevent us from silently standardizing those figures. For the pending fixture, derive an expected output from the current authorized specification and explicit dummy inputs. Keep that planned check separate from any retrospective investigation of the practice sheet's disputed annotations.

A tester followed the patched archive link on staging and reached the expected rehearsal scoreboard. Their note includes both renamed rows and the destination heading. The route defect can close for that build. We have not deployed the page publicly. The event coordinator wants the unresolved receipt case kept off the public standings even if the display infrastructure is ready.

That provides the missing observed link behavior for the identified staging build. Public deployment remains a separate authorization, and the outstanding receipt decision is not repaired by a working page. A release checklist can therefore show the presentation route as checked while preserving the data-readiness hold. The stable identifiers in the test note make the verification more specific than a generic page loaded report.

The second witness has acknowledged the E14 request but asked for the original rather than the scan because the ink near the time field is faint. The archive custodian can arrange an inspection but has not scheduled it. We should not mark the witness unavailable indefinitely, nor write that they confirmed the carbon-copy explanation. Their message is a request for better evidence, not a chronology decision.

The next action is to arrange access to the original and retain the scan comparison as preparation. A dated appointment would be useful if agreed, but the current record does not contain one. We can list the custodian as the contact for arranging inspection without inventing a booking. Keep the unresolved timestamp and signature questions in the inspection request so the meeting has a concrete purpose.

The calculator reviewer has now documented the text-input error: the workbook stops calculation and highlights the cell, with a message to enter a number or leave it blank for pending. The coordinator accepted that validation behavior. Numeric zero is still awaiting its own run because the review machine used a cached copy with an older test sheet. We have not claimed any result from that unsuitable copy.

Accepting the error message closes the operator-response question for the tested build. The zero boundary case still requires the intended workbook and fixture version. Before running it, compare version labels and the relevant formula cells rather than relying on the file name alone. Otherwise a successful calculation on the wrong copy could be recorded against a repair it never exercised.

The latest operator handoff file has a missing attachment icon where the approved input-convention page should appear. The prose still refers to that page. I stopped distribution and restored the attachment from the approved document folder, but I have not opened the packaged handoff on another computer. The training attendance note remains in place and should not be reset because of this packaging defect.

Treat the missing attachment as a delivery-package issue. Restoring a file prepares a remedy; opening the actual package elsewhere would test whether the recipient can access it. The earlier operator's understanding evidence remains valid within its scope. We can preserve that evidence while ensuring the next recipient gets the approved convention instead of a broken reference.

The custodian has offered two possible times for viewing the original E14 sheet, but neither witness has selected one. I have sent the options onward and saved the message as an offer, not a confirmed appointment. The requested comparison remains the original time field against the carbon copy and the witness explanation of when each mark was added. No new receipt order decision arrived today.

For the immediate handoff, list arranging the joint inspection as the open action and include the evidence links. Do not mark a time slot booked merely because the custodian can provide access. If only one witness attends, note that limitation rather than silently treating the comparison as the combined sign-off. The existing resolved early-sheet collision need not be reopened unless new evidence concerns it.

A new operator noticed that calc-c's test sheet was protected against editing, so the planned zero-input fixture could not be entered without a password. The maintainer has supplied a test-only unlocked copy and its checksum. Nobody has yet run the fixture on that copy. This is a concrete access obstacle to the remaining test, not evidence that zero behaves incorrectly in the calculator.

The next reviewer can verify the supplied checksum and formula equality, enter the defined fixture, and record the result. Those are proposed steps, not work I have performed. Keep the protected operational workbook intact while using the designated test copy. An unlocked copy should not automatically become the production artifact just because it is more convenient for a boundary check.

The packaged operator handoff was opened on a second computer today. The approved convention attachment opened, but its document title did not include the version letter, so the recipient asked which revision it represented. The file contents match the approved page by checksum. I asked the maintainer to add version metadata to the package index; that small presentation edit is not yet delivered.

The observed attachment access repairs the missing-file problem. The remaining index clarification can be tracked without discarding the checksum match or pretending the document content is unknown. A recipient-facing index should identify the approved version and its scope. It should not imply that opening the document completes calculator testing or resolves the receipt chronology; those workstreams have separate evidence.

I added a delivery checklist item requiring the archive page to stay labeled rehearsal until the coordinator separately approves publication. There is no new public standings file in this packet. The last staging route test remains the relevant infrastructure evidence. Today's checklist is a proposed release safeguard, not a record of a public deployment or a result for any competing team.

I can turn this packet into a scoped administrative note using the current authorized policy and independently available receipt requirements. Its next action should name an unresolved check with the evidence needed, not manufacture completion from a prepared patch, an offered appointment or an unlocked test copy. Historical practice material stays historical; future rule changes would need an explicit effective event before controlling current calculations.

haystack_sessions.content: This is our fictional community quilt exhibition ledger. The sealed reserve for quilt Q7 is 240 fictional credits. It is a threshold in the internal bid paperwork, not a public catalog asking price. I need three workstreams tracked separately: the object's technique description, the protective wrapper and transport fit, and registration-stub reconciliation. None of this script represents an actual sale or real person's property.

I would keep the internal threshold ledger separate from the public object labels. The public readiness work can proceed from technique evidence and physical handling checks without exposing bid thresholds. For each workstream, a useful handoff distinguishes a proposed remedy, an approved design and an observed check. Combining those statuses under a single ready box would conceal which evidence is still missing.

Our first Q7 description says entirely hand sewn. The maker's questionnaire instead says the front pieces were assembled on a machine and the layered quilt was stitched by hand. I copied both descriptions into a discrepancy note rather than correcting the questionnaire. The introductory wall panel uses handmade in a broader sense, so the same word there does not answer this particular construction question.

The questionnaire supports a more specific technique description than the broad phrase on the wall panel. I suggest asking the maker to confirm how we describe the separate assembly and quilting stages. A general handmade label might remain acceptable as introductory language, but it should not override a precise object label. We have a disagreement in wording, not evidence that the maker misreported the process.

The packing volunteer requested an acid-free wrapper large enough to fold around Q7 without pulling at the corners. The supplier's first message confirms material type but gives no usable dimensions. Our storage worksheet has the folded quilt dimensions from a measured handling trial, but the wrapper order sheet was filled from a generic stock description. We have not received or fitted any wrapper yet.

Material confirmation and dimensional fit are different requirements. The next order review should compare the actual stock dimensions with the measured folded object and the planned overlap. I can draft a checklist, but that would not establish fit before the item arrives. Keep the handling trial measurement attached to Q7; measurements from another exhibit should not become its packing specification by proximity.

Registration includes two stubs labeled B16. One belongs to the earlier desk pad and one to the afternoon pad; neither sheet lists a bidder's name in the public sequence field. The private clerk ledger can connect each stub to a participant code. I have not resolved those associations. A general materials-budget note elsewhere lists 240 credits for display boards, which is unrelated to any quilt's sealed reserve.

The repeated budget number does not make the display-board allocation a reserve copy. Its object, purpose and ledger are separate. For the registration collision, retain both physical stubs and their pad origins before editing the participant-code map. A public sequence list can use disambiguated stub references without publishing the internal participant correspondence or any sealed threshold from the bid ledger.

The maker has approved this Q7 label requirement: distinguish hand quilting from machine piecing. Their reply explicitly explains that the top was machine pieced and the quilting stitches through the layers were done by hand. They did not approve a claim that every stitch anywhere on the object was hand made. I filed the reply with the object-description revision and left the broader wall panel unchanged pending its separate review.

The object label can use that approved distinction without guessing more about construction. A proofreader should check that a line break or compressed caption does not collapse the two stages into entirely hand sewn again. The maker's approval applies to this wording and this object. It does not certify every technique description on the wall panel or substitute for a later print-quality check.

I have created a private reserve breakdown sheet for Q7. Its first allocation row is base 150 credits and its second allocation row is contribution 90 credits; the heading says these two entries together make up Q7's sealed reserve. Those are not the transport budget or opening bid. The sheet is stored with the protected ledger, while the display-board budget remains in the general supplies folder.

The two protected allocation rows are a reconstructive representation of the same Q7 threshold because the sheet names their shared reserve role. Reading only a generic credits legend would not establish that relation. A downstream internal note using either allocated component should retain the ledger's access scope. Nothing about that breakdown grants permission to publish a reserve or to renegotiate it.

The supplier sent wrapper dimensions today. The width is smaller than the overlap required by the folded-object measurement in our handling worksheet. I told the packing volunteer to pause the fit plan and ask whether a larger sheet is available. The original order was already dispatched, so a cancellation may not stop delivery. We should not label the requested larger sheet received or installed.

A dimensional mismatch can be documented before delivery without inventing a physical trial. The immediate next step is to obtain the alternative stock dimensions and determine whether a replacement order is possible. If the original sheet arrives, retain its packing label as evidence of what was supplied. Do not mark its material unsuitable merely because its dimensions fail the planned wrap geometry.

The registration clerk found that the earlier B16 stub belongs to participant code P-elm and the afternoon B16 stub belongs to P-reed. Their initials are on both supporting sign-in lines. I changed the internal draft map to include pad origin beside the stub number. The clerk has not yet signed the corrected map, so this is an evidence-based draft association awaiting the specified clerical acknowledgment.

The sign-in lines provide a basis for the proposed correction, while the missing acknowledgment remains a separate workflow status. Public sequence labels can distinguish morning-pad B16 and afternoon-pad B16 without exposing participant codes. Before publishing even that sequence list, check that its order derives from the appropriate registration evidence and not from alphabetic sorting of those new labels.

The first label proof arrived as a PDF. Its wording matches the maker's approved technique distinction, but the two lines are stacked so closely that a quick reading joins machine with quilting. I asked the designer to increase spacing and retain an explicit punctuation break. The proof is a layout artifact, not the original construction evidence. We can fix readability without reopening what the maker reported.

A revised layout should be checked both against the approved words and as a reader would encounter it at viewing distance. Correct tokens alone do not guarantee an unambiguous phrase. I suggest a small proof log recording which version was inspected, at what size, and what was observed. A visual check described in that log is still distinct from approval of the object's technique facts.

The undersized wrapper arrived. The packing volunteer measured the sheet on an empty table and confirmed the supplier dimensions. They did not place Q7 in it, because the planned overlap was already impossible. The material label says acid free, but we have no independent laboratory verification of that claim. Our current record is supplier-labeled material and observed sheet size, not a conservation certification.

Keep that evidence at its actual level: a measured sheet and a supplier declaration. A replacement request can cite the observed dimension mismatch without overstating a material failure or performing an unnecessary wrap trial. We can retain the unused sheet for another appropriate task only after checking that task's requirements. It should not be silently substituted for Q7's still-needed wrapper.

The clerk signed the corrected participant-code map for the two B16 stubs. I compared both signed entries with the preserved sign-in lines and found the mapped codes match. This resolves that specific pair. A separate stub B19 has an illegible suffix, and the clerk has asked its holder to confirm the code. The confirmation request has been sent, but there is no reply yet.

Close the duplicated B16 association with the signed map as evidence, while leaving B19 open. Treat the unanswered holder request as an action taken, not a confirmed identity. A sequence list can include B19's position if its ordering evidence is clear, but it should not silently infer the participant code from adjacent entries. Order and identity association are separate fields in the registration workflow.

The display-board supplies invoice has now arrived. Its total differs from the earlier budget because a smaller pack was ordered, and the treasurer filed it as an ordinary material expense. It does not update any reserve entry. The expense receipt and Q7 reserve breakdown have different document identifiers and storage permissions. I want the handoff to keep those distinctions even if a summary discusses both finances.

A general readiness note can state whether supplies have arrived or a material expense is recorded without disclosing a protected threshold. Equal or different amounts across documents do not determine dependency; their meanings do. The reserve breakdown remains bound to its quilt and internal bid purpose, whereas the board invoice supports an independent supplies workflow. A single finance heading should not erase those evidence boundaries.

The designer sent label proof two with a punctuation break and more space between the construction stages. On the screen it is easier to read, and the maker replied approved wording after seeing the text transcript. They did not inspect a printed proof. I asked the print volunteer for an actual-size sample. That sample has been requested, not produced, and the previous cramped PDF remains in the revision folder.

The maker's reply confirms the words, while the pending physical sample will test the presentation. A readiness checklist should keep those approvals separate. If the printed label later loses the punctuation or compresses the lines, the transcript approval would not excuse that defect. I would attach the approved transcript and the PDF version identifier to the print request so the intended comparison is explicit.

The supplier offered a larger wrapper with dimensions matching the plan and asked us to confirm the order. I have approved the replacement order using the packing volunteer's dimensional worksheet. The dispatch notice has not arrived. Do not treat the offered product photograph as evidence of the delivered material or a successful fit around the folded quilt; it is only a catalog image.

There is now authorization for a replacement order and evidence of its stated dimensions. Arrival, label inspection and fit remain future checks. When the parcel comes, match its identifier to the approved order before using it, because a dimensionally similar package could contain the original stock. The handling worksheet remains the reference for fit, rather than the supplier photograph's apparent scale.

The public registration-sequence draft accidentally included a hidden spreadsheet column containing the private participant codes. The visible printout looked acceptable, but the shared file would reveal the codes if that column were unhidden. I withdrew the draft link and exported a new table with only public stub references and order. I have not yet checked the exported file's metadata or hidden objects.

The withdrawal addresses availability of the mistaken draft; it does not prove every copy disappeared. The replacement export needs its own inspection for hidden fields and retained data. Keep a record of which link was withdrawn and who was asked to replace it, without claiming a remote deletion we cannot observe. This registration exposure is separate from the sealed reserve, which was never included in that draft.

A visitor-services volunteer suggested putting a starting price on every object label to reduce questions at the desk. I have not approved that suggestion. Q7's public label has no price field, and its sealed reserve must not be mistaken for a catalog offer. The volunteer has received a proposed response that staff can explain the bidding procedure without supplying individual internal thresholds.

The suggestion is a proposal about public presentation, not new permission to disclose protected ledger values. We can give staff a neutral explanation of the process using public rules, while leaving object-specific thresholds in authorized internal use. It is important not to convert the absence of a public price into a statement that the object has no internal reserve or that bidding is already open.

The physical label sample arrived, but it was printed from the first PDF. The cramped two-line phrase is back. The print volunteer confirmed that an older file remained in their queue. I rejected that sample for display and provided the second proof's identifier and approved transcript again. No one has yet printed the corrected sample, so wording approval cannot be counted as physical-label readiness.

This shows a version-delivery failure rather than disagreement about technique. A useful repair is to remove the stale job from the active queue and request a new sample with its source version recorded on the back. I would still preserve the rejected sample in the evidence packet. It demonstrates how an approved digital revision can fail to reach the actual display artifact.

The larger wrapper has been dispatched, according to a tracking message that names our replacement order. It is expected to arrive at the storage room, but there is no signed receipt. The packing volunteer is available to inspect it once received. Availability does not mean an inspection has happened. Our transport checklist therefore still shows wrapper fit unresolved, even though the order and dispatch steps are documented.

The task can advance from waiting for dispatch to waiting for receipt and fit. A tracking message is useful evidence for shipment status, but it cannot establish the contents, condition or suitability of the parcel. The volunteer's availability can be used to plan the check without inventing a fixed appointment. Record the actual received sheet dimensions and the observed overlap when the check occurs.

We inspected the public-sequence export with a spreadsheet viewer and found no hidden columns or additional worksheets. A text extraction from the file also contained only stub references and sequence numbers. The file still had an author-name property copied from the clerk's workstation. Our publication policy requires a generic exhibition author field, so I asked for that metadata correction before release.

Those inspections support the absence of the checked data fields in the examined export, not a universal claim about every past file or viewer. The author property is a separate remaining release issue. A revised export should receive a fresh identifier so its metadata check can bind to the actual file we intend to publish. Keep the withdrawn draft distinct from the inspected public-only table.

The holder of B19 replied with a photograph of their stub, but the suffix is obscured by a finger. The message also states a participant code in text. The clerk has not accepted that self-report as sufficient to alter the signed ledger. They asked for a clearer photograph and a comparison with the desk copy. We should not write that B19's code has now been verified.

A reply has arrived and contains a claim, but the requested corroboration remains incomplete. The next step can name the exact missing evidence instead of saying simply follow up. A clearer image and the desk copy may establish the suffix; if they conflict, retain both rather than replacing one silently. The closed B16 mapping does not provide evidence for this distinct stub.

The corrected label sample was printed from proof two and its source identifier appears on the back. The print volunteer compared the words with the transcript and found no missing phrase. A second reader has not checked it at the intended display distance. I accepted the version and transcription check while leaving the second-reader presentation check pending. The sample is stored separately from the rejected first version.

The new physical sample has stronger provenance and a completed transcription comparison. It still needs the independent readability observation requested in the exhibition workflow. A second reader should describe how they interpret the two stages rather than merely say looks fine. That gives us evidence about the earlier ambiguity without requiring them to know the intended answer before reading the label.

The replacement-wrapper parcel reached storage and the custodian signed for it. The external package label matches the new order. The inner sheet has not been unfolded because the inspection table was occupied by another object. This is receipt evidence only. We have not measured the delivered sheet or compared its folds with Q7; the physical-fit task remains outstanding despite the correct outer label.

The custodian's signature and outer-label match close the arrival step. The next check needs a clear handling area and the object-specific worksheet. Do not infer inner contents from the parcel label alone. If the inspection must wait, record the obstruction rather than turning the waiting period into a failed fit result. No observation of overlap exists until the sheet is actually examined in the planned configuration.

The clerk revised the export's author property and sent a checksum for version public-sequence-c. I compared its visible rows with the previously inspected table and found no change. I have not opened the metadata panel myself. The clerk says it is corrected, but our release checklist asks for a separate verification. The public link has not been activated while that final check remains open.

The unchanged visible rows support continuity of sequence content, while metadata correction is still a reported action awaiting the specified check. A reviewer can open the exact file identified by the checksum and inspect the author property. Using an older download would not verify the revised export. The release decision should name the tested version and avoid claiming the withdrawn draft was globally erased.

A new internal note abbreviated the protected Q7 allocation sheet as base plus contribution, pointing back to its two original entries. It did not print their numbers in the note. I kept that note in the internal ledger folder because its linked rows reconstruct the threshold. The public object label and public sequence export do not carry that link; they support independent tasks without access to it.

The linked note is semantically dependent on the reserve breakdown even without an amount written inline. Access control needs to follow that evidenced link, not merely search for a numeral in the note. At the same time, an unrelated materials worksheet using the words base and contribution would not automatically inherit this relation. The specific Q7 ledger reference is what establishes the dependency here.

The second label reader visited the display mock-up and correctly described machine assembly of the top and hand stitching through the layers. Their report names proof two and the viewing distance. That completes the requested interpretation check for this sample. The installation volunteer then noticed that the label holder's edge covers the final punctuation when the sample is inserted fully. We have not checked a modified holder yet.

The reader result remains valid for the unobstructed sample; the holder creates a new presentation defect in the installed configuration. It would be misleading to erase the successful test or to let it certify a condition it did not include. A proposed remedy is to adjust the insert depth or holder geometry, then inspect the actual installation. Record which remedy is tried instead of silently trimming approved text.

The packing volunteer cleared the inspection table but found a tear in the wrapper's outer shipping sleeve. The inner folded sheet appears intact through the opening, though it has not been fully unfolded. They asked whether to photograph the sleeve before opening it. I approved documenting the packaging condition first. No conclusion about the wrapper's functional fit or cleanliness has been made from that partial view.

Photographing the packaging can preserve useful delivery evidence before handling changes it. Then the designated volunteer can inspect the actual sheet according to the handling plan. A torn shipping sleeve does not itself prove the inner wrapper unusable, and a glimpse of an intact fold does not prove the entire sheet sound. Keep condition and dimensional-fit observations separate when they are eventually recorded.

The metadata reviewer opened public-sequence-c by its checksum and confirmed the generic exhibition author property. They found no private-code field in the reviewed rows or document properties. The coordinator approved that export for public release. The web volunteer has not yet activated its link, so the file is approved but not observed publicly accessible. The internal reserve ledger remains outside this export workflow.

Approval supports the intended release of the identified public-only file. Activation still needs an observed web check if the handoff must say available. Nothing in this approval expands access to the separate reserve notes. A public sequence list can be ready while a physical wrapper or installed label is not; the exhibition readiness note should preserve those independent statuses rather than use one global green flag.

The B19 desk copy has been located, and its suffix is clearer than the first photograph. The clerk thinks it matches the holder's typed code but has requested the holder's unobscured image before signing the correction. We now have stronger evidence but not the completed acknowledgment. I linked the desk-copy scan in the open item and retained the earlier obscured photograph as part of the correspondence history.

That is progress in evidence quality, not yet closure under the clerk's stated process. The next follow-up can request the specific unobscured view and compare it against the new desk scan. A summary should not say no evidence exists, because the desk copy is available; equally, it should not say the identity was signed off. Both overstatements would misrepresent the current task state.

Today the holder's second photograph arrived and shows the full B19 suffix. The clerk compared it with the desk copy and drafted a corrected association entry. Their acknowledgment signature is missing from the saved page, apparently because the scan captured only its front. I requested the reverse page before treating the draft as the completed signed ledger update. The participant's public sequence position is unchanged.

The two matching images support the proposed association, but the missing signature page keeps the procedural confirmation open. A targeted next step is to obtain the reverse scan and bind it to this correction page. Do not ask the participant to start the evidence process again unless a genuine mismatch appears. The unresolved point is now acknowledgment evidence, not the legibility problem that initiated the case.

The installation volunteer made a spacer for the label holder. An empty paper strip can now sit clear of the edge, but the approved Q7 sample has not been inserted for the check. The volunteer left the spacer next to the holder with a note saying ready to try. That wording describes a prepared remedy, not proof that the label's technique distinction is visible after installation.

The next inspection should use the actual approved sample in the modified holder and confirm the full phrase remains readable. The earlier reader report helps identify the intended distinction, but cannot substitute for this new installed-state observation. If the spacer works, record the tested holder and sample versions. If it fails, keep the failed trial evidence rather than rewriting the prior approval history.

The wrapper sleeve has been photographed and the inner sheet unfolded. No tear was observed in the exposed sheet. Its measured dimensions match the replacement order. The volunteer stopped before fitting it around Q7 because the quilt was still in the photography area. We have a completed sheet inspection and dimension check, but no completed object-specific overlap or fold trial.

A sensible handoff action is to arrange the fit trial when the quilt returns, using the measured sheet and the existing folding worksheet. Do not repeat receipt as if the parcel were still missing, and do not claim transport readiness from sheet dimensions alone. The remaining check concerns the actual folded object and handling arrangement, which the latest session has explicitly not tested.

The web volunteer activated the approved public-sequence link and recorded its page title and file checksum. I can therefore mark that publication step observed for this version. The same message asks whether the visitor-services desk should distribute printed technique labels before installation is checked. I have not approved early distribution; the question is a new proposal, not a change to any sealed reserve permission.

The readiness note can separate the published sequence from the remaining physical-display and packing checks. It should choose a concrete open action from the current evidence and leave proposed early distribution awaiting a decision. Internal financial content is available only within its granted scope; public craft description and handling tasks remain useful without it. No activity here establishes a completed bid, sale or transfer of the fictional object.
